**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 647, MAP2+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D visualization of both regenerating/remodeling axons and mature/residual axonal scaffolds across a 15-mm-long fixed rat spinal cord segment—a dense, lipid-rich CNS tissue. uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for long-range projections in large CNS specimens (T06 tier), offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we use immunolabeling: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels all neuronal processes including regenerating axons, while MAP2 specifically marks dendritic and somatic cytoskeletons of mature neurons, enabling distinction between axonal regeneration (TUJ1+) and neuronal structural integrity/survival (MAP2+). Both Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 are highly compatible with uDISCO and provide spectrally separable, photostable signals ideal for light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for spinal cord to reduce autofluorescence)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) + anti-MAP2 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five more times, total 6 washes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) + donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-immunolabeling Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 five more times, total 6 washes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, DiI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity visualization of long-range axonal projections across the entire CNS (35–40 mm), demanding a clearing method with strong delipidation power, deep dye penetration, and compatibility with lipophilic tracers and antibody-based labeling. uDISCO is established for whole-body and long CNS samples, provides high refractive index matching for deep imaging, and preserves signals from both DiI (a lipophilic carbocyanine dye ideal for tracing neuronal projections over millimeters to centimeters) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated antibodies. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we avoid GFP/YFP reporters and instead use exogenous DiI injection (pre-fixation or post-fixation pressure injection into cortex) combined with pan-axonal immunostaining against β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)—a robust marker of neuronal processes—to distinguish specific labeled projections from the global axonal scaffold. This dual-labeling strategy enables unambiguous identification of corticospinal tract fibers against background neuroanatomy.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if tissue pigmentation interferes)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (for β-III Tubulin)  
3.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 1 hour each at RT.  
3.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100) + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201) diluted 1:500 in PBST + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 6 buffer changes)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (H+L), diluted 1:300 in PBST + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 6 buffer changes)  

7 Dehydration (post-staining)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in light-protected glass vial at RT. Sample is ready for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. DiI signal (Ex/Em ~549/565 nm) and Alexa Fluor 647 (Ex/Em ~650/668 nm) can be imaged sequentially with minimal crosstalk.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 488, MBP+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D visualization of long-range corticospinal projections across the entire CNS (≈40 mm), demanding a clearing method with strong delipidation power, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with robust synthetic fluorophores. uDISCO is established for whole-body and long-CNS samples (T06 tier), provides excellent transparency in lipid-rich neural tissue, and preserves Alexa Fluor dyes effectively. Endogenous FPs are quenched by solvent-based methods, so we avoid GFP/YFP reporters and instead use immunolabeling: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels all neuronal axons (including corticospinal tracts) with Alexa Fluor 488 for green-channel projection mapping; MBP (myelin basic protein) with Alexa Fluor 647 labels myelinated tracts in red/far-red to delineate white matter architecture and assess spatial relationships between projecting fibers and endogenous myelinated pathways. This dual-target strategy enables continuous tracing of unmyelinated/myelinated segments along the entire path while preserving structural context.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for CNS pigmentation)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201, 1:500) and anti-MBP (e.g., Abcam ab7349, 1:300) diluted in PBT + 5% NDS + 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat 6.1 five more times (total 6 washes, 6 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% NDS + 0.01% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)  

8 Post-labeling Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes, 6 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term storage <1 month)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for long CNS segments (T06 tier), offering strong delipidation power, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes—critical for preserving the structural integrity of fragile spinal cord injury tissue while enabling long-range axonal tracing. Unlike electrophoresis-based methods (e.g., CLARITY variants), uDISCO avoids mechanical stress that causes tissue fragmentation. The dual-labeling strategy targets pan-neuronal cytoskeletal components: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels all axons (including regenerating fibers), while MAP2 marks dendrites and somata, allowing discrimination between axonal projections and neuronal cell bodies across injury core, rostral, and caudal regions. Both markers are compatible with uDISCO’s organic solvent environment when paired with Alexa Fluor 568/647, which resist quenching and provide high signal-to-noise for deep imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing PBT every 1–2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Total Time: 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Total Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.4 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥24 hours)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Mount sample in a glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with DBE, ensuring no air bubbles and maintaining longitudinal orientation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, MBP + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity visualization of long-range axonal projections from cortex to spinal cord and their spatial relationship with myelinated white matter tracts. uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for large, dense CNS samples (35–40 mm), offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. It achieves high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging of intact CNS. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we use immunolabeling: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels all neuronal axons (pan-neuronal structural marker) to trace projection paths, while MBP (myelin basic protein) labels myelinated tracts to serve as anatomical reference for white matter pathways. Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red) and Alexa Fluor 488 (green) are both highly compatible with uDISCO and minimize spectral crosstalk during multichannel imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for CNS pigmentation)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-MBP (1:250) diluted in PBST + 5% normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) diluted in PBST + 5% normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-labeling Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.3 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final clearing and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Mount sample in a glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with DBE, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 647, DiI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for long-range projection tracing in intact mammalian CNS, offering high refractive index matching, strong lipid removal, and superior preservation of exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes and lipophilic tracers (e.g., DiI). Unlike the user’s prior organic-solvent protocol that skipped critical intermediate steps, FDISCO includes graded dehydration, controlled delipidation, and RI-matching with dibenzyl ether (DBE), minimizing tissue shrinkage while maintaining fluorescence. The dual-labeling strategy uses DiI for anterograde/retrograde tracing of specific long-range projections (ideal for cortex-to-spinal cord pathways) and pan-axonal β-III Tubulin immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 647 to visualize the endogenous axon scaffold as spatial reference—both compatible with FDISCO’s chemistry and resistant to quenching. This combination enables unambiguous discrimination between target projections and background fiber tracts across the entire 35–40 mm CNS axis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for CNS pigmentation)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) mouse monoclonal antibody diluted 1:500 in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day with 6 buffer changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG diluted 1:500 in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day with 6 buffer changes)  

9 DiI Tracer Application (if not pre-injected; otherwise skip)  
9.1 Pressure-inject or crystal-apply DiI at cortical target site; incubate in 4% PFA at 37 ℃ for 2 weeks to allow diffusion along axons.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 14 days)  

10 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Repeat incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

13 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Store sample in 100% (vol/vol) DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
13.2 Mount sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 (anti-Aβ) + Alexa Fluor 647, NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques across the entire 5XFAD mouse brain, demanding deep antibody penetration, strong lipid removal for optical clarity in dense tissue, and compatibility with quantitative volumetric imaging. iDISCO+ is an established organic solvent–based clearing method optimized for whole adult mouse brains (~10 mm scale), offering rapid, high-clearing power with minimal residual autofluorescence—critical for detecting sparse Aβ deposits. It supports robust immunolabeling with covalently conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes (e.g., AF647 and AF488), which are compatible with iDISCO+ and resistant to quenching during dehydration and delipidation. 6E10 specifically recognizes human Aβ1–16, enabling precise plaque detection in 5XFAD mice; NeuN (RBFOX3) provides a pan-neuronal reference channel for anatomical registration and regional normalization of plaque density. Nuclear counterstains like DAPI are avoided due to poor compatibility and non-specificity for the target.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for 5XFAD to reduce lipofuscin)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-6E10 (1:500) and anti-NeuN (1:300) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG1 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) and donkey anti-mouse IgG2a conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300), diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 2:1 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer cleared brain into glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 + Alexa Fluor 488, 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for whole adult mouse brains (5–12 mm scale) with high lipid content and dense pathology like Aβ plaques in 5XFAD models. It enables deep antibody penetration, strong delipidation for high transparency, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488 and 568—both validated as compatible fluorophores in iDISCO+. Using two well-characterized anti-Aβ monoclonal antibodies (6E10 targeting Aβ<sub>1–16</sub>, 4G8 targeting Aβ<sub>17–24</sub>) labeled with spectrally distinct but iDISCO+-compatible dyes allows direct spatial comparison of Aβ deposition patterns across cortical and hippocampal regions without reliance on endogenous fluorescence (which iDISCO+ quenches). This dual-epitope strategy provides orthogonal validation of plaque identity, morphology, and regional burden in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 4 buffer changes)  
6.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: anti-mouse IgG1 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500, for 6E10) and anti-mouse IgG2b conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500, for 4G8), diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 4 buffer changes)  
8.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer cleared brain into glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term; up to 2 weeks recommended for optimal signal)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 + Alexa Fluor 488, 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for whole adult mouse brains (5–12 mm), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for dense amyloid-laden AD tissue. It provides high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging and effectively clears lipofuscin-like autofluorescence that could confound plaque detection. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as we use exogenous immunolabeling. The dual-antibody strategy targets Aβ with two well-validated monoclonal antibodies: 6E10 (recognizes Aβ<sub>1–16</sub>) and 4G8 (recognizes Aβ<sub>17–24</sub>), labeled with spectrally distinct, iDISCO+-compatible fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488 and 647). This cross-validation minimizes false positives from non-specific aggregates or autofluorescence, enabling robust 3D quantification of plaque burden across brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for AD brain to reduce lipofuscin)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (wt/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 4 buffer changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), diluted in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 4 buffer changes, protected from light)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 2:1 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial for long-term storage/imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for adult mouse brain and tumor tissue, offering strong delipidation power for dense samples (~8 mm scale), excellent preservation of vascular morphology, and compatibility with both Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647—critical for dual-channel imaging of endothelial barrier integrity (Claudin-5) and pan-vascular labeling (Lectin). Unlike iDISCO+, FDISCO preserves fluorescence intensity better during dehydration and RI matching, and it supports deep antibody/dye penetration without quenching these synthetic fluorophores. Lectin provides robust, perfusion-independent labeling of the entire vasculature (including tumor neovasculature), while Claudin-5 specifically marks tight junctions of the blood-brain barrier, enabling direct spatial comparison of barrier continuity between tumor core, margin, and healthy parenchyma.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Claudin-5 primary antibody (1:200 in blocking buffer) + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum, 50 µg/mL) in PBST + 5% serum + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat PBST wash 5 times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Dehydration (post-staining)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Store sample immersed in ECi at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
10.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for adult mouse brain and tumor tissue up to ~10 mm, offering strong delipidation power for dense GBM samples while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes and exogenous lectin labeling. It enables deep penetration of antibodies and lectins into thick tissue blocks and achieves high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) labels functional vasculature lumen with high specificity and signal-to-noise in cleared tissue, while Claudin-5—a tight junction protein specific to brain endothelial cells—reports blood-brain barrier integrity. Dual labeling with Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red, stable in FDISCO) and Alexa Fluor 488 (green, compatible per method-fluorophore matrix) allows simultaneous 3D mapping of vascular architecture and barrier continuity across tumor core, invasive front, and normal parenchyma.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented GBM; include if sample shows hemorrhage/melanin)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Claudin-5 primary antibody (1:200 in PBST + 5% donkey serum) and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., IB4, 10 µg/mL) simultaneously.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times with fresh PBST, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  

7 Secondary Labeling and Streptavidin Conjugation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat or anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated streptavidin (1:500) in PBST + 5% donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-labeling Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four times with fresh PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 647, Congo red + TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for whole adult mouse brains (5–12 mm), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for detecting dense Aβ plaques in deep brain regions like the hippocampus. It preserves Alexa Fluor 647 and TO-PRO-3 fluorescence effectively, while quenching endogenous FPs (irrelevant here as labeling is exogenous). The dual-target strategy uses 6E10/4G8 (Aβ-specific monoclonal antibodies) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 for high-specificity immunodetection, and Congo red—a classic amyloid-binding dye—with TO-PRO-3 as a nuclear counterstain that also enhances Congo red’s contrast via spectral separation and tissue context. Both fluorophores are compatible with iDISCO+, enabling mutual validation of plaque distribution, morphology, and spatial load without relying on endogenous reporters.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction in aged AD brain)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (6E10 / 4G8)  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody mix: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 10% DMSO + 5% normal goat serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washes Post Primary  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two additional times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Washes Post Secondary  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two additional times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

9 Congo Red and TO-PRO-3 Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with Congo red (0.05% wt/vol in PBS) + TO-PRO-3 (1:1000) in PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

10 Post-Staining Washes  
10.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
10.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

11 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
11.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Delipidation  
12.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
12.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
12.3 Repeat step 12.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

13 Refractive Index Matching  
13.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
13.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

14 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
14.1 Store cleared brain in 100% DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
14.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for dense adult mouse brain tissue with high lipid content (such as GBM-infiltrated regions), offering strong delipidation power while preserving endogenous fluorescence and—critically—exogenous dye signals like Alexa Fluor conjugates and lectin. Unlike CUBIC (aqueous, slow, causes swelling and structural disintegration in tumor-rich regions), FDISCO minimizes morphological distortion in heterogeneous tumor-brain interfaces and maintains vascular continuity. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) robustly labels perfused vasculature across tumor and normal brain, while Claudin-5—a tight junction protein specific to blood-brain barrier endothelial cells—enables assessment of barrier integrity. Both markers are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent workflow and Alexa Fluor dyes retain brightness post-clearing. This dual-labeling strategy directly addresses the need to map tumor-vessel spatial relationships, vascular density/branching, and BBB structural continuity in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS containing 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Claudin-5 primary antibody (1:200 in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 changes, 24 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  

4 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-staining  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat/mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Lectin (10 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

5 Post-staining Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (3 changes, 24 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Delipidation and Bleaching  
7.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed per constraints)  
*(Skipped per problem constraints—no additional markers beyond specified)*  

9 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh change) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Sigma-Aldrich, 112372) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Store sample immersed in 100% ECi at RT in the dark until imaging (stable for ≥2 weeks)  
10.2 Mount in glass-bottom dish filled with ECi for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.558)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP) in sparse neurons while resolving fine dendritic morphology. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves endogenous GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence, minimizes tissue distortion, and supports deep antibody penetration—critical for immunolabeling structural markers like MAP2 in 3 mm brain blocks. MAP2 specifically labels dendrites and soma of mature neurons, complementing sparse endogenous GFP to enhance visualization of dendritic arborization without masking the genetically defined neuronal population. MACS achieves high transparency in thick slices within ~2 days with low toxicity, enabling long-term storage and repeated imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST: 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to fresh MACS-R2 in airtight imaging-compatible glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for storage)  
3.2 Equilibrate at least 2 hours in MACS-R2 before imaging to ensure RI homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 For long-term storage (>1 month), replace MACS-R2 monthly to prevent microbial growth and maintain fluorescence stability (Temperature: 4 ℃, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP/YFP) in 3 mm thick mouse brain blocks, along with high-fidelity labeling of dendritic morphology. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method that is fully compatible with endogenous GFP fluorescence, minimizes tissue distortion, enables deep antibody penetration into dense brain tissue, and supports long-term sample stability—critical for 6-month archival. Among structural neuronal markers, MAP2 specifically labels dendrites (including fine branches and spines) without nuclear or axonal cross-reactivity, making it ideal for complementing sparse reporter neurons. Alexa Fluor 488 is highly compatible with MACS, photostable, and spectrally aligned with GFP for co-imaging or signal reinforcement.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash tissue 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or rabbit, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST, then 2 × 1 hour in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: as indicated)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer cleared tissue to fresh MACS-R2 in airtight, light-protected glass vial. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite storage up to 6 months)  
3.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours to ensure optical homogeneity. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The sample contains weak endogenous GFP signal that must be preserved over 6 months, ruling out solvent-based methods (e.g., uDISCO, iDISCO+) that quench fluorescent proteins. Among aqueous, FP-compatible clearing methods established for 3 mm brain blocks (MACS, Ce3D, ScaleS, FOCM), MACS offers the best balance of rapid clearing (~1–2 days), excellent endogenous FP preservation, deep antibody penetration, minimal tissue distortion, and compatibility with long-term storage in high-RI aqueous media. MAP2 is a well-validated pan-neuronal dendritic marker that complements sparse GFP+ neurons by revealing full dendritic arborization without interfering with endogenous GFP. Alexa Fluor 488 is spectrally distinct from GFP but compatible with standard filter sets and shows high photostability and retention in MACS. This dual-labeling strategy ensures that even if endogenous GFP fades slightly during storage, the MAP2-AF488 channel provides robust structural backup for dendrite tracing, while GFP retains cell-type specificity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 × 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 × 2 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash, dark)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle shaking)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue to fresh MACS-R2 in airtight, light-protected glass vial with minimal headspace (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite up to 6 months)  
3.2 Prior to imaging after storage: equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours in the dark to restore optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample consists of fixed 3 mm mouse brain blocks with weak endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP) that must be preserved for long-term storage and repeated imaging. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves endogenous fluorescence (including GFP), enables deep antibody penetration in thick tissue, minimizes morphological distortion, and uses low-toxicity reagents—making it ideal for longitudinal studies requiring structural fidelity over 6 months. To complement sparse endogenous GFP-labeled neurons and resolve dendritic arborization, we co-label with anti-MAP2 (a dendritic cytoskeletal marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, which is compatible with MACS and provides high-contrast structural context for tree complexity and local circuit analysis without interfering with GFP signal.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash tissue 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST, then 2 × 1 hour in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer cleared tissue into fresh MACS-R2 in glass vials with PTFE-lined caps. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)  
3.2 Store samples at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 6 months. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 180 days)  

4 Pre-Imaging Equilibration (prior to each imaging session)  
4.1 Gently rinse sample once in fresh MACS-R2 to remove surface precipitates. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
4.2 Mount directly in MACS-R2-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method established for dense human clinical brain tissue (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), enabling deep antibody penetration and effective delipidation of myelin-rich cortex. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 conjugates, which resist quenching during dehydration and organic solvent steps. NeuN provides robust nuclear labeling of mature neurons, while MAP2 labels somatodendritic compartments—dual structural signals enhance neuron identification reliability in 3D across cortical layers and perilesional zones. Although uDISCO causes mild shrinkage, it preserves overall cytoarchitecture sufficiently for quantitative spatial analysis in thick (5 mm) slices.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented human tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-labeling Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term; image within 1 week for optimal signal)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** Human cortical tissue (5 mm thick, dense, high lipid/myelin content) requires a high-clearing-power solvent-based method. uDISCO is established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK, provides deep antibody penetration, effectively removes lipids and myelin, and achieves high transparency in days rather than weeks. Although it quenches endogenous FPs, our labeling uses exogenous Alexa Fluor-conjugated antibodies, which are fully compatible with uDISCO. NeuN (RBFOX3) is a well-validated pan-mature-neuronal nuclear marker, while MAP2 labels neuronal dendrites—providing complementary structural information for 3D neuron mapping, layer analysis, and density quantification. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are robustly preserved in uDISCO.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for human tissue with pigments)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (chicken polyclonal, 1:500) in staining buffer (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% DMSO + 5% normal donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing buffer every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-chicken IgG (1:500) in staining buffer (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% DMSO + 5% normal donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing buffer every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP from sparse neuronal labeling) while complementing with a structural marker to delineate dendritic arbors for spine density normalization. MACS is an aqueous, fast, low-toxicity clearing method established for ≤500 μm brain slices, fully compatible with GFP and Alexa Fluor dyes, and enables deep antibody penetration without quenching or significant tissue distortion. MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic shaft marker that labels the somatodendritic compartment robustly, enabling accurate reconstruction of dendritic length and branching—critical for spine density normalization. Alexa Fluor 568 provides bright, photostable red emission spectrally separable from GFP, with excellent compatibility in MACS.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 × 30 min) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 min) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Transfer slices into imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 (RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min equilibration)  
3.2 Mount between #1.5 coverslips using spacer-compatible silicone gasket or metal frame to avoid compression (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)
