**Chosen Method:** FOCM  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires rapid (<1 day) transparentization of 500 μm fixed mouse brain slices while preserving endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP from sparse neuronal labeling) and enabling high-resolution imaging of dendritic spines. FOCM is an aqueous, fast, low-toxicity clearing method specifically validated for thin brain slices (≤500 μm), with excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescence (GFP/YFP/tdTomato) and minimal tissue distortion—critical for accurate spine density quantification. To enhance dendritic shaft visualization and distinguish neuronal morphology beyond sparse GFP labeling, we pair endogenous GFP with immunostaining for MAP2 (a dendrite-specific cytoskeletal marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568, which is fully compatible with FOCM and provides robust, stable signal without quenching. This dual-labeling strategy ensures reliable identification of dendritic arbors and spines across experimental groups.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (performed before clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 × 30 minutes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with FOCM  
2.1 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution A: 10% (wt/vol) fructose + 5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution B: 25% (wt/vol) fructose + 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution C: 40% (wt/vol) fructose + 15% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with FOCM RI-Matching Solution: 60% (wt/vol) fructose + 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0 (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Transfer slices into glass-bottom imaging chamber or mounting slide with a drop of FOCM RI-Matching Solution and cover with #1.5 coverslip (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for ≤48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves 3 mm thick, densely fixed human cortical tissue where deep antibody penetration failed with aqueous PBS-based labeling. uDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense human clinical brain blocks (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching that enables deep antibody penetration and uniform labeling throughout millimeter-scale tissue. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 conjugates—robust synthetic fluorophores resistant to organic solvents—and supports dual-pan-neuronal structural labeling: NeuN (nuclear marker of mature neurons) and MAP2 (dendritic/somatic marker), providing complementary signals to reliably identify mature neurons in deep layers. Endogenous fluorescence is not required (no GFP/YFP transgenes in human tissue), so quenching by uDISCO is irrelevant. The method’s dehydration and delipidation steps enhance antibody diffusion far beyond the 1 mm limit observed with PBS-only incubation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for human tissue with lipofuscin)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat 6.1 five more times (total 6 washes, 6 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-labeling Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes, 6 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat 10.2 once (fresh DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The original TDE protocol failed due to excessive concentration (100% directly), lack of gradual refractive index (RI) matching, and methanol-based fixation that likely compromised membrane integrity and endogenous fluorescence. For 500 μm brain slices requiring rapid (<24 h), high-fidelity clearing with preserved endogenous GFP signal and clear visualization of dendritic spines, an aqueous, FP-friendly method is essential. MACS is established for thin brain slices (≤500 μm), preserves GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence, enables deep antibody penetration, minimizes tissue distortion, and completes within hours at RT. MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic shaft marker that complements sparse GFP-labeled neurons by outlining the full dendritic arbor, enabling accurate spine density normalization per unit dendrite length. Alexa Fluor 488 is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from GFP if needed, though often used to amplify or confirm dendritic structure when endogenous signal is sparse.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation and Methanol Removal  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to reverse methanol-induced artifacts and stabilize morphology.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

2 Immunolabeling for Dendritic Skeleton  
2.1 Blocking with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody against MAP2 (e.g., mouse anti-MAP2, 1:500 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
2.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated secondary antibody (1:800 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

3 Optical Clearing with MACS  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MNDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MNDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MNDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer cleared slice into imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate confocal or light-sheet imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging within 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for small whole embryonic samples (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescence (though not required here), deep antibody penetration, minimal tissue distortion, and compatibility with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 568. The dual-labeling strategy targets early neuronal processes (β-III Tubulin/TUJ1, a pan-neuronal marker labeling all axons and neurites) and neural crest–derived glial/precursor lineages (Sox10, critical for cranial/spinal/peripheral nerve development). This combination enables reliable identification of both neuronal projections and their associated support cells during E12.5 neurogenesis, fulfilling the need for dual structural validation of early nerve trajectories.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Labeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:500) and anti-Sox10 (1:300) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 4 changes, 2 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash, protected from light)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A1: 25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-A2: 50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B: 80% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to Ce3D-M: 88% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (RI ≈ 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Store and image in Ce3D-M at 4 ℃ in sealed glass vials, protected from light (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite for imaging within 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for small whole embryonic samples (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of delicate early neural projections. It supports deep penetration of antibodies and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 fluorophores. The dual-labeling strategy targets both pan-neuronal processes (via β-III Tubulin/TUJ1, a well-validated marker for developing axons and neurites in E12.5 embryos) and neural crest-derived glial/precursor populations that guide cranial and spinal nerve pathfinding (via Sox10). This combination enables simultaneous visualization of neuronal trajectories and their associated support cells across the entire embryo, fulfilling the goal of mapping continuous nerve paths and analyzing spatial projection patterns.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: total 48 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: total 48 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution A: 10% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (NMN), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution B: 25% (wt/vol) NMN, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution C: 40% (wt/vol) NMN, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-RI Matching Solution: 63% (wt/vol) iodixanol in PBS (final RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with fresh Ce3D-RI Matching Solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, HuC/D + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole embryonic samples (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of delicate early neural projections. It supports deep antibody penetration and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes. The dual-labeling strategy targets both early differentiating neurons (β-III Tubulin/TUJ1 labels all post-mitotic neurons and their nascent neurites) and more mature neuronal somata/axons (HuC/D marks committed neuronal nuclei and proximal processes), enabling simultaneous visualization of immature outgrowths and established nerve bundles across head, trunk, and periphery. This overcomes the prior failure caused by insufficient antibody incubation and inadequate washing; extended cold incubations and rigorous washes in Ce3D buffer dramatically reduce background while enhancing signal depth.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Primary Antibody Incubation  
1.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:500) and anti-HuC/D (1:500) diluted in Ce3D Ab Dilution Buffer (Ce3D-A: 25% w/v fructose, 10% w/v urea, 0.5% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS) supplemented with 5% v/v normal goat serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

2 Washing  
2.1 Wash with Ce3D Wash Buffer (Ce3D-W: 25% w/v fructose, 10% w/v urea, 0.5% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Repeat wash with fresh Ce3D-W. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.3 Repeat wash with fresh Ce3D-W. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) diluted in Ce3D Ab Dilution Buffer with 5% v/v normal goat serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

4 Post-Labeling Washing  
4.1 Wash with Ce3D-W. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
4.2 Repeat wash with fresh Ce3D-W. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
4.3 Repeat wash with fresh Ce3D-W. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Final wash with Ce3D Clearing Buffer (Ce3D-C: 50% w/v fructose, 20% w/v urea, 0.5% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-C. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Transfer to fresh Ce3D-C for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Store cleared embryo in Ce3D-C at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. Prior to light-sheet or confocal microscopy, equilibrate sample in Ce3D-C at RT for 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃ for storage; RT for pre-imaging equilibration, Time: storage indefinite; pre-imaging: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous-based, insect-optimized clearing method specifically validated for Drosophila whole heads and brains (~0.5 mm), preserving fine synaptic ultrastructure with minimal distortion—critical for resolving spatial organization of synaptic domains. It maintains endogenous fluorescence but is also fully compatible with antibody-based labeling using Alexa Fluor dyes. Bruchpilot (nc82) is the gold-standard marker for Drosophila presynaptic active zones, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters adjacent to active zones; dual immunolabeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 enables precise discrimination of active zone cores versus surrounding vesicle pools. FlyClear supports deep antibody penetration in chitin-rich Drosophila cuticle without harsh solvents, avoiding quenching or shrinkage seen in organic methods like uDISCO/iDISCO+, which is essential for quantitative 3D synapse mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with FlyClear-A: 25% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.4 (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FlyClear-B: 50% (wt/vol) fructose, 25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.4 (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FlyClear-C: 70% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.4 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with FlyClear-M: 80% (wt/vol) fructose, 35% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.4 (final RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish in fresh FlyClear-M (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for whole-mount embryonic samples (~8–10 mm), providing strong delipidation and high refractive index matching for deep imaging of both large nerve tracts and fine neurites. It preserves exogenous fluorescent dyes (e.g., Alexa Fluor conjugates) while quenching endogenous FPs—thus requiring antibody-based labeling. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) robustly labels all developing neuronal processes, including early extending axons and mature bundles, while Sox10 specifically marks neural crest-derived lineages that give rise to cranial/spinal peripheral nerves, enabling dual visualization of structural continuity and lineage identity. Both primary antibodies are well-penetrating in embryos and compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent workflow. FDISCO also supports low background and high signal-to-noise for long-range 3D tracing in light-sheet microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigments present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (e.g., R&D Systems AF2864, 1:200) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

8 Post-labeling Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer embryo to glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary filled with BABB (1:2) for immediate light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging within 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous-based, insect-optimized clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and fine synaptic ultrastructure while effectively clearing chitinous cuticle in Drosophila heads. It enables deep antibody penetration into intact ~0.5 mm samples without significant shrinkage—critical for accurate 3D mapping of synaptic domains. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a well-established marker for the presynaptic active zone in Drosophila, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters; dual immunolabeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes (488/568) provides high-contrast, photostable signals compatible with FlyClear’s mild conditions and ideal for high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to ensure complete fixation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, Developmental Studies Hybridoma Bank) at 1:50 and rabbit anti-Synapsin (Synaptic Systems #101 002) at 1:200 in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

4 Primary Antibody Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Secondary Antibody Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour, protected from light)  

7 Dehydration (Optional Pre-Clearing Step for Cuticle Penetration)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

8 Rehydration  
8.1 Reverse methanol series: 80%, 50%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  
8.2 Final wash in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 FlyClear Optical Clearing  
9.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

10 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
10.1 Transfer samples to fresh FlyClear Solution B for final RI matching (RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
10.2 Mount cleared heads in glass-bottom imaging chambers filled with FlyClear Solution B, oriented for optimal brain access. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous-based, insect-optimized clearing method specifically validated for intact Drosophila brains and heads (~0.5 mm), preserving fine synaptic ultrastructure with minimal distortion—critical for quantifying synapse density, cluster size, and spatial correspondence between active zones and vesicle pools. It maintains endogenous fluorescence but, more importantly, supports deep and uniform antibody penetration without organic solvents that could damage delicate synaptic architecture. Bruchpilot (nc82) is the gold-standard marker for Drosophila presynaptic active zones, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters; dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes (488/568) enables high-resolution 3D mapping of their spatial relationship. Both antibodies are well-established in Drosophila neuroscience and compatible with FlyClear’s mild, non-denaturing conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Primary Antibody Incubation  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100): 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per change)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per change)  

5 Clearing (FlyClear Protocol)  
5.1 Incubation with FlyClear-A: 25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with FlyClear-B: 50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with FlyClear-C: 75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
6.1 Incubation with FlyClear-M: 88% (wt/vol) fructose, 40% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (final RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh FlyClear-M (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous, insect-optimized clearing method specifically validated for Drosophila heads and brains, preserving fine synaptic structures while effectively clearing the chitinous cuticle—a key failure point in the user’s prior SeeDB2 attempt. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., uDISCO, iDISCO+), FlyClear maintains endogenous protein epitopes and is compatible with standard immunofluorescence, avoiding fluorescence quenching. The chosen markers—Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) for the presynaptic active zone and Synapsin for synaptic vesicle clusters—are well-established, target-specific antibodies in Drosophila neuroscience. Paired with Alexa Fluor 488 and 568, they provide spectrally distinct, photostable signals compatible with FlyClear’s aqueous environment and high-resolution 3D imaging. The protocol includes extended permeabilization and antibody incubation to ensure deep penetration into cuticle-enclosed tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) for enhanced permeabilization and blocking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) diluted in PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

5 Post-Staining Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

6 Tissue Clearing with FlyClear  
6.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (20% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 5% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (40% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution C (60% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) sucrose, 15% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like P7 mouse calvarial bone, enabling deep antibody penetration into mineralized regions while achieving strong transparency with minimal residual autofluorescence. It effectively quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins but preserves dye- and antibody-conjugated fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor 488/568—ideal for dual immunolabeling of early (Osx) and mature (Osteocalcin) osteoblast lineage markers. This strategy allows precise spatial discrimination of progenitor vs. differentiated cells across suture mesenchyme, osteogenic fronts, and bone plates. FDISCO’s relatively fast protocol and compatibility with bone tissue make it superior to slower aqueous methods (e.g., Ce3D) for this application, and its organic solvents efficiently suppress bone autofluorescence that could confound signal detection.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 three more times, total of 4 washes.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-goat IgG (1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-Staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 three more times, total of 4 washes.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (Post-Labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)  
11.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for hard mineralized tissues like P7 mouse calvaria, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for dense bone. It effectively reduces bone autofluorescence in the green-red channels while preserving Alexa Fluor dye signals. Osx (Osterix) marks early osteoprogenitors/pre-osteoblasts, whereas Osteocalcin labels mature, matrix-embedded osteoblasts—enabling spatial discrimination across suture zones. Both targets are compatible with antibody-based labeling and Alexa Fluor conjugates under FDISCO conditions, avoiding reliance on endogenous fluorescent proteins (which FDISCO quenches). This strategy minimizes background, supports deep penetration into 2-mm-thick bone blocks, and preserves 3D architecture with acceptable shrinkage for quantitative spatial analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Autofluorescence Quenching  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 1% normal donkey serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS), 6 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  

5 Post-Staining Washes  
5.1 Wash with PBST, 6 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in sealed container for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like postnatal mouse calvarial bone, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging of mineralized tissue. It enables excellent penetration of antibody-conjugated fluorophores and preserves signal from synthetic dyes despite quenching endogenous fluorescent proteins—irrelevant here as labeling relies on immunostaining. Osx (Osterix) marks early osteoprogenitors/pre-osteoblasts, while Osteocalcin labels mature osteoblasts/osteocytes, enabling spatial discrimination of differentiation stages across suture zones. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum*) labels vasculature to assess angiogenesis in the suture microenvironment. All three fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568/647) are compatible with FDISCO and provide spectrally resolvable channels for multiplexed 3D analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200), anti-Osteocalcin (1:200), and *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin (10 µg/mL), all diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing buffer every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit IgG (1:400, for Osx), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse IgG (1:400, for Osteocalcin), and no secondary needed for Lectin-Alexa Fluor 568 (pre-conjugated), all diluted in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing buffer every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, stored over molecular sieves).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 ratio, RI ≈ 1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with BABB.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like intact mouse bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody penetration into the mineralized femur and efficiently clears lipid-rich marrow while preserving dye-based fluorescence. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so we use immunolabeling with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes. Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the bone marrow niche, and CD31 (PECAM1) robustly labels vascular endothelial cells—enabling precise 3D mapping of neuro-vascular spatial relationships within the hematopoietic stem cell microenvironment. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are fully compatible with FDISCO chemistry.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone marrow autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-TH (e.g., rabbit anti-TH, 1:200) and anti-CD31 (e.g., rat anti-CD31, 1:100) diluted in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 2% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, with gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, total washing time: 6 hours  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 2% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, total washing time: 6 hours  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer cleared femur to a glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary filled with DBE, orient sample as needed for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in DBE for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like intact mouse femur, enabling deep antibody penetration into the bone marrow cavity while preserving fine neural and vascular structures. It efficiently removes lipids and decalcifies minimally fixed bone without severe distortion, critical for spatial analysis of the hematopoietic niche. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes. Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the bone marrow, and CD31 (PECAM1) robustly labels vascular endothelial networks—both are well-established targets in hematopoietic stem cell niche studies. Dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 allows high-contrast, low-crosstalk 3D imaging of nerve–vessel spatial relationships across central marrow, endosteal, and metaphyseal regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if residual pigmentation observed)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each at RT.  
3.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:300) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Post-staining Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  

7 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation and Clearing  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

10 Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Mount sample in a glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with DBE, sealed to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves transparentizing intact, mineralized mouse femur—a hard tissue with high clearing difficulty—while preserving delicate bone marrow cavity architecture and enabling dual-channel imaging of sympathetic nerve fibers (target: tyrosine hydroxylase, TH) and vascular/vascular-pericyte structures (target: CD31/PECAM1). BoneClear caused excessive brittleness during叔丁醇 dehydration, likely due to harsh solvent-induced demineralization and dehydration stress. Ce3D is an aqueous-based, morphology-preserving clearing method established for hard tissues (T07 tier), offering deep antibody penetration without organic solvents that cause fragility. It maintains endogenous fluorescence compatibility but here uses robust Alexa Fluor–conjugated antibodies, which are fully compatible with Ce3D. TH is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in bone marrow; CD31 labels endothelial cells of vasculature, enabling reconstruction of vascular networks and perivascular niches. This combination avoids nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) that do not contribute to structural mapping and aligns with compatibility cautions in the knowledge base.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Staining (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle rotation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat (1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle rotation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A1 (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-A2 (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Matching Solution (Ce3D-B supplemented with 0.5% (wt/vol) agarose for sample support if needed) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Mounting in glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with Ce3D-Matching Solution, oriented for longitudinal or cross-sectional femur imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for dense hard tissues like intact mouse femur (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA tier). It enables deep antibody penetration into the mineralized bone and marrow cavity while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes such as Alexa Fluor conjugates. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so we use immunolabeling with target-specific primary antibodies: tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) to label sympathetic nerve fibers and CD31 (PECAM1) to mark vascular endothelial structures—both validated markers for bone marrow neuro-vascular microenvironment studies. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are FDISCO-compatible, photostable, and spectrally separable for dual-channel 3D imaging of nerve-vessel spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-TH (rabbit or goat, 1:200) and anti-CD31 (rat or hamster, 1:100) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host-IgG (for TH, 1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-host-IgG (for CD31, 1:400) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-labeling Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with BABB (1:2 vol/vol) and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor 488, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for dense mineralized tissues like the cochlea within the otic capsule. It effectively decalcifies and delipidates hard bone while enabling deep penetration of small-molecule dyes and antibodies—critical for accessing spiral-shaped cochlear structures buried in bone. Unlike BoneClear (which failed to fully clear bone or preserve signal), FDISCO provides superior transparency of bony matrices and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, specific marker for both inner and outer hair cells; Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles without requiring genetic reporters; TO-PRO-3 serves as a far-red nuclear counterstain with minimal background in cleared tissue and compatibility with FDISCO. This combination enables simultaneous identification of hair cell identity, stereocilia integrity, and spatial mapping across cochlear turns—all essential for noise-damage gradient analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling and Cytoskeletal Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
1.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated secondary antibody (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
1.6 Incubation with TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Decolorization and Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 vol 30% H₂O₂ + 5 vol MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Repeat incubation with fresh DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of DCM and dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (Sigma, #108014) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Final incubation with fresh 100% DBE for imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with DBE, seal tightly (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
5.2 Mount in custom DBE-compatible chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging recommended)

FDISCO—a solvent-based, fluorescence-preserving variant of DISCO—is established for hard tissues like bone and cochlea, offering rapid and effective delipidation and decalcification-like clearing without full demineralization, while maintaining spiral morphology. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so direct labeling with small-molecule probes or antibody-conjugated fluorophores is required. Phalloidin specifically labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles of both inner and outer hair cells with high contrast and structural fidelity, enabling precise identification of hair cell position and integrity. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, hair cell-specific cytoplasmic marker that complements Phalloidin by labeling the entire hair cell soma, allowing unambiguous distinction between inner and outer hair cells based on morphology and spatial arrangement. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are compatible with FDISCO and provide spectrally separable, photostable signals ideal for 3D reconstruction and automated counting.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Repeat step 2.2 with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Immunolabeling and Phalloidin Staining  
3.1 Rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 minutes each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
3.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibody against Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking buffer) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:50 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
3.4 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes over 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
3.5 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.6 Wash thoroughly with PBST, 4 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Repeat step 4.5 with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Bleaching (optional, if autofluorescence present)  
5.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours in dark)  
5.2 Wash with 100% methanol, 2 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) BABB (Sigma-Aldrich, B6630).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.3 Transfer sample to fresh 100% BABB in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store cleared cochlea in 100% BABB at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term; up to 1 week recommended for optimal signal)  
7.2 Mount sample in BABB-filled glass-bottom dish or capillary for light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring minimal air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires distinguishing pan-neuronal (泛神经) fibers from sympathetic-specific fibers within the dense, mineralized environment of intact mouse molars. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) and tyrosine hydroxylase (TH, a specific marker for sympathetic neurons) are well-established target-specific markers for this purpose. Since endogenous fluorescent proteins are not mentioned and hard dental tissue demands strong delipidation and high refractive index matching, FDISCO—a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for hard tissues like teeth—is optimal. It enables deep antibody penetration, preserves Alexa Fluor dye signals (compatible per knowledge base), and achieves rapid, high-contrast clearing without requiring genetic reporters. Aqueous methods (e.g., MACS, Ce3D) are less effective for dense mineralized matrices, while FDISCO’s organic solvents efficiently remove lipids and match RI in hard tissues.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Labeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-TH (1:250) diluted in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 2 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 2 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 vol 30% H₂O₂ + 5 vol methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, dark)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol: 2 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

4 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Sigma-Aldrich, 112302) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with fresh 100% ECi (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for dense hard tissues like the bony cochlea (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep penetration of dyes and antibodies into mineralized bone-encased spiral structures while preserving fine F-actin architecture. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses direct chemical probes: Phalloidin (which directly binds F-actin in stereocilia bundles without requiring antibodies) and an anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (a hair cell-specific marker). TO-PRO-3 provides nuclear counterstain compatible with FDISCO and does not interfere with Myosin VIIa or F-actin signals. This combination allows simultaneous visualization of hair cell identity (Myosin VIIa), apical actin cytoskeleton (Phalloidin), and cellular morphology (nuclei), fulfilling all scientific goals including gradient analysis along the cochlear spiral.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Decalcification (optional but recommended for cochlear bone)  
2.1 Incubation with 1:1 mixture of methanol and dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling and phalloidin staining)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.5% DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in PBST + 5% NGS) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 in same buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with fresh PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Nuclear Counterstaining  
7.1 Incubation with TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 in PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Bleaching (optional, if autofluorescence persists)  
10.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

11 Final Dehydration  
11.1 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
12.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
12.3 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ≈ 1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.4 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until imaging)
