**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is a dense, mineralized hard tissue embedded in the otic capsule, requiring a high-clearing-power method with deep dye/antibody penetration. FDISCO—a solvent-based, FP-quenching but dye-compatible protocol—is established for hard tissues like bone and cochlea, offering rapid, strong delipidation and refractive index (RI) matching suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging of intact spiral structures. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin–rich stereocilia bundles without antibodies, enabling high-resolution visualization of bundle integrity; Myosin VIIa is a specific marker for cochlear hair cells, allowing precise identification and quantification along the tonotopic axis; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cell counting and spatial registration. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568, DAPI) are compatible with FDISCO per knowledge-base records.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (Myosin VIIa)  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody (e.g., Proteus Biosciences #25-6790, 1:200) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin/DAPI Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated secondary antibody (1:500), Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100), and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes).  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with pure ethyl cinnamate (ECi, RI ≈ 1.558).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The target is the complete trajectory of pulp nerve fibers in an intact mouse molar—a dense, mineralized hard tissue requiring strong delipidation and high refractive index (RI) matching. FDISCO is a solvent-based method established for hard tissues (T07 tier), offering rapid, deep clearing with excellent preservation of fine neural architecture and compatibility with lipophilic tracers (e.g., DiI) and antibody-based labeling (e.g., PGP9.5). DiI provides direct, diffusion-based anterograde/retrograde labeling of neuronal membranes from the root apex without requiring genetic models or complex immunostaining for all fibers, while PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) ensures comprehensive labeling of total nerve fibers, including non-DiI-penetrated branches. Both are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent environment and do not rely on endogenous fluorescence (which FDISCO quenches). This dual-labeling strategy maximizes coverage of the entire pulp innervation pattern while preserving 3D morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-clearing Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Neural Tract Tracing with DiI  
2.1 Microinjection or focal crystal placement of DiI (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate; 5 mg/mL in ethanol) at the root apex under stereomicroscope. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes application)  
2.2 Incubation in PBST to allow DiI diffusion along nerve fibers. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  

3 Post-tracing Fixation  
3.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to stabilize DiI labeling. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

6 Rehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Immunolabeling for PGP9.5  
7.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-PGP9.5 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation)  
7.3 Washing with PBST (3 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each wash)  
7.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse or anti-rabbit IgG (1:400 dilution in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  
7.5 Washing with PBST (3 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each wash)  

8 Dehydration (post-immunolabeling)  
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Clearing and RI Matching  
9.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB; 1:2 vol/vol). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.4 Incubation with final RI-matching solution: ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with ECi for long-term storage at RT, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
10.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, MBP + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample includes dense mineralized bone, soft muscle, and peripheral nerves—requiring a high-clearing-power method compatible with thick, heterogeneous hard tissues. FDISCO is established for T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA, provides strong delipidation and deep dye penetration, and preserves fluorescence of exogenous dyes like Alexa Fluor conjugates. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels the entire peripheral nerve network, while MBP (myelin basic protein) specifically highlights myelinated, large-diameter fibers—enabling simultaneous visualization of total nerve architecture and myelinated subsets. Both antibodies are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent-based protocol and yield robust signal in dense tissue after permeabilization.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.8 Rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
1.9 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.10 Incubation with blocking solution (PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-MBP (1:300) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PBST (6 changes over 3 days, 12 hours per change).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle agitation)  

5 Post-staining Washes  
5.1 Wash with PBST (6 changes over 3 days, 12 hours per change).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for hard, dense tissues like teeth (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA tier), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging of mineralized samples. It preserves synthetic fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor dyes) while quenching endogenous FPs—irrelevant here since we use exogenous labeling. PGP9.5 is a pan-neuronal marker highly specific for dental pulp nerves, enabling robust visualization of nerve fibers throughout the pulp chamber. Phalloidin labels F-actin in soft tissue cytoskeleton, delineating pulp stromal boundaries and overall pulp morphology. This dual-labeling strategy fulfills the scientific goal: PGP9.5 reveals 3D nerve architecture in central pulp, pulp horns, and apical foramen regions, while Phalloidin outlines soft tissue contours without requiring nuclear counterstains that could obscure fine neural processes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for teeth to reduce autofluorescence)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-PGP9.5)  
5.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated secondary antibody (1:400) + Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes).  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary tube filled with BABB (1:2 vol/vol) for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or short-term storage <7 days at 4 ℃ in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, DiI]  
**Justification:** The sample includes mineralized vertebral bone, cartilage, and dense muscle—classified as high-clearing-difficulty hard tissue (T07 tier). FDISCO is a solvent-based, FP-quenching method specifically established for this tissue tier, offering strong delipidation and deep dye penetration while preserving exogenous dye fluorescence. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are not required per the problem statement; instead, direct labeling of the entire peripheral nerve network is needed. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal cytoplasmic marker) paired with Alexa Fluor 647 provides robust, specific labeling of all axons in nerve roots and branches. Complementary DiI (a lipophilic carbocyanine dye) enables long-range tracing of fine nerve processes through bone foramina and muscle interstices without requiring antibody penetration into dense regions. Both dyes are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent environment and exhibit excellent signal retention post-clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-labeling Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling (for PGP9.5)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal, 1:500) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

3 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 DiI Bulk Tracing (applied after immunolabeling to avoid interference)  
4.1 Microinjection or focal crystal placement of DiI (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate) at proximal nerve root entry zones using glass micropipette or fine forceps.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate application)  
4.2 Incubation in PBS with 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide to allow DiI diffusion.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 14 days in dark)  
4.3 Post-DiI wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (two changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

6 Delipidation and Bleaching  
6.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) in 100% methanol (prepared from 30% H₂O₂ stock: 1 vol H₂O₂ + 5 vol MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Wash with 100% methanol (two changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Organic Solvent Transition  
7.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) mixture of methanol and dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (two changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Final incubation in fresh 100% DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in glass vial wrapped in aluminum foil at RT.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term; replace DBE weekly for long-term)  
9.2 Mount in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.56).

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The sample contains dense mineralized bone and muscle, requiring a high-clearing-power solvent-based method. FDISCO is established for hard tissues (T07 tier), enables deep penetration of antibodies and dyes, and preserves fluorescence of synthetic fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 647/488—critical since endogenous FPs are not specified. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a target-specific pan-neuronal marker for peripheral nerve fibers, while Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in muscle fibers without needing an antibody, satisfying the requirement to prioritize small-molecule structural probes for spatial reference. This dual-labeling strategy allows simultaneous 3D visualization of nerve trajectories and muscle architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated Phalloidin (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat once)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Rehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Dehydration (Second Round)  
7.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat once)  

8 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, repeat once)  
8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Sample Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to fresh DBE in glass vial with PTFE-lined cap.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage)  
9.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous mCherry fluorescence from breast cancer cells while achieving whole-body transparency in an adult mouse—a large, lipid-rich sample. Among established whole-body clearing methods, MACS is aqueous-based, fully compatible with red fluorescent proteins (including mCherry/RFP), and supports deep antibody penetration without quenching. To distinguish true epithelial tumor micro-metastases from autofluorescent background or non-specific particles, we supplement the endogenous signal with immunostaining against Pan-Cytokeratin (a pan-epithelial marker highly specific for carcinoma cells) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, which is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from mCherry. This dual-labeling strategy enhances specificity and confidence in single-cell metastasis detection across diverse organs.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and 0.3 M glycine in PBS to reduce autofluorescence and enhance antibody access.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Blocking with MACS-Blocking Buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.02% NaN₃ in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., clone AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in MACS-Blocking Buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
2.3 Washing with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (3 changes, 24 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) in MACS-Blocking Buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
2.5 Final wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (3 changes, 24 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  

3 Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer to final RI-matching solution: MACS-R2 supplemented with 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide for long-term storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite; store in dark)  
4.2 Equilibrate sample in imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, MBP + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample consists of dense hard tissue (vertebrae with mineralized bone and cartilage) combined with muscle and peripheral nerves—requiring a high-clearing-power method that penetrates lipid-rich and calcified matrices while preserving fine neural morphology. FDISCO is established for T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA, provides strong delipidation and decalcification-compatible processing, enables deep antibody penetration, and preserves far-red fluorescence (Alexa Fluor 647). Endogenous FPs are quenched in solvent-based protocols like FDISCO, so we avoid reliance on GFP/YFP and instead use validated target-specific immunolabeling: PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker for all peripheral nerve fibers) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, and MBP (myelin basic protein, specific for myelinated axons/nerve tracts) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647. This dual-labeling strategy fulfills the goal of visualizing both泛神经 networks and myelinated structures without introducing non-listed fluorophores or markers. FDISCO’s methanol/H2O2-based bleaching step effectively suppresses bone autofluorescence—a key issue noted in the problem statement—while maintaining structural integrity for 3D spatial analysis of nerve trajectories relative to bony foramina and muscle.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 5% (wt/vol) BSA.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Immunolabeling  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-MBP (1:300) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
5.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) in blocking buffer (omit serum if secondaries are pre-absorbed).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.4 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (4 changes, 2 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

6 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with BABB for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
8.2 Mount in BABB-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional RI adjustment.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (endogenous), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous mCherry/RFP fluorescence in a whole adult mouse for systemic micro-metastasis screening, combined with epithelial tumor cell validation via immunostaining. Among established whole-body clearing methods, MACS is aqueous-based, preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including mCherry/RFP), enables deep antibody penetration into dense tissues, and minimizes morphological distortion—critical for accurate single-cell quantification and spatial analysis. Pan-Cytokeratin is a well-validated pan-epithelial marker that specifically labels carcinoma cells (including breast cancer) and is compatible with MACS when paired with Alexa Fluor 647, which exhibits high stability and minimal quenching in this system. This dual-channel strategy (mCherry + Pan-Cytokeratin-AF647) ensures reliable identification of true micro-metastatic foci while excluding false positives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Pan-Cytokeratin primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat washing buffer incubation (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Repeat washing buffer incubation (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  

6 Post-Staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
6.2 Repeat washing buffer incubation (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
6.3 Final wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

7 Optical Clearing with MACS  
7.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for long-term storage and light-sheet/confocal imaging (Temperature: 4 ℃, protected from light; stable for ≥4 weeks)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous mCherry/RFP fluorescence from tumor cells across the entire adult mouse body, including dense tissues like bone and brain. Among established whole-body clearing methods, MACS is aqueous-based, non-denaturing, and explicitly compatible with mCherry/RFP and Alexa Fluor dyes, avoiding the FP-quenching effects of solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). Pan-Cytokeratin serves as a target-specific epithelial tumor identity marker to confirm mCherry+ signals are bona fide carcinoma cells and not autofluorescent artifacts or non-epithelial RFP+ debris. Alexa Fluor 647 is chosen for its deep-tissue compatibility, photostability, and spectral separation from mCherry, enabling dual-channel validation of micro-metastases in complex organs.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (Pan-Cytokeratin)  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Pan-Cytokeratin primary antibody diluted 1:200 in antibody dilution buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

4 Washing After Primary Antibody  
4.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 three times with fresh wash buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (or appropriate host species) diluted 1:400 in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing After Secondary Antibody  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 three times with fresh wash buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Optical Clearing with MACS Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Transfer sample to final imaging medium: MACS-R2 (same as 7.3) in glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage at RT, protected from light)  
8.2 Equilibrate for at least 12 hours before imaging to ensure uniform RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous mCherry/RFP signal in a whole adult mouse, which rules out solvent-based methods that quench fluorescent proteins (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). Although CUBIC is aqueous and FP-compatible, it suffers from insufficient hemoglobin removal in poorly perfused whole bodies—exactly the issue described. MACS is an established aqueous method for whole adult mice that effectively clears hemoglobin-derived pigments while preserving endogenous red FPs like mCherry and enabling deep antibody penetration. Pan-Cytokeratin is a validated epithelial tumor cell marker suitable for detecting breast cancer micrometastases across organs and is compatible with MACS when paired with Alexa Fluor 647, which resists quenching and provides orthogonal validation to mCherry without spectral overlap. This dual-channel strategy (mCherry + Pan-CK-AF647) enables specific micrometastasis identification while excluding autofluorescence or heme artifacts.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Initial Wash (assumed completed but critical for success)  
1.1 Transcardial perfusion with ice-cold PBS (10–15 mL) followed by 4% PFA in PBS (20–25 mL).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: perfusion at ~2 mL/min)  
1.2 Post-fixation in 4% PFA in PBS overnight.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)  
1.3 Wash in PBS with 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

2 Hemoglobin Removal and Decolorization  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-Bleach solution (5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash in PBST three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

3 Tissue Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (NMN), 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40% (vol/vol) NMN, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40% (vol/vol) NMN, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  

4 Immunolabeling for Epithelial Validation  
4.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBS) for permeabilization and blocking.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (mouse monoclonal, e.g., clone AE1/AE3) diluted 1:200 in antibody dilution buffer (1% NGS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
4.3 Wash in PBST six times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours each)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:400 in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
4.5 Wash in PBST six times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours each)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with MACS-Matching Solution (60% (vol/vol) NMN, 60% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Final equilibration in fresh MACS-Matching Solution for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging  
6.1 Store sample immersed in MACS-Matching Solution at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
6.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy with dual-channel detection: mCherry (Ex/Em ≈ 587/610 nm) and Alexa Fluor 647 (Ex/Em ≈ 650/665 nm) for micrometastasis mapping at single-cell resolution.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically optimized for dense, pigmented, and lipid-rich tissues like melanoma. It provides strong delipidation and depigmentation capacity while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes. Given the high melanin content in the tumor—which causes severe light absorption and scattering—FDISCO’s organic solvent system effectively reduces pigment interference and enables deep imaging of vascular networks. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) binds specifically to glycoproteins on the luminal surface of endothelial cells, providing rapid, uniform, and target-specific labeling of the entire perfusable vasculature without requiring lengthy antibody penetration. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly compatible with FDISCO, exhibits minimal quenching, and offers excellent signal-to-background in the far-red channel, which is less affected by residual melanin absorption. This combination avoids reliance on endogenous fluorescent proteins (which are absent here) and bypasses the need for additional endothelial markers like CD31, as lectin alone suffices for complete vascular mapping per the problem constraints.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Tissue Preparation (assumed completed; included for protocol completeness)  
1.1 Transcardial perfusion with ice-cold PBS followed by 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 minutes perfusion each)  
1.2 Dissection of intact subcutaneous melanoma (8–10 mm diameter) and post-fixation in 4% PFA.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Vascular Labeling with Lectin  
2.1 Wash tissue 3× in PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
2.2 Incubation with 50 µg/mL *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in PBST.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
2.3 Wash tissue 5× in PBST to remove unbound lectin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Delipidation and Depigmentation  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) in 100% methanol (prepared from 30% H₂O₂ stock: 1 vol H₂O₂ + 5 vol MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Rehydration (optional intermediate step for FDISCO compatibility; omitted per standard FDISCO protocol—proceed directly to dichloromethane)  
5.1 [Skipped – FDISCO transitions directly from methanol to DCM]  

6 Organic Solvent Transition  
6.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) mixture of 100% methanol and dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112302).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Transfer to fresh 100% ECi for final clearing and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours or until optically transparent)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount cleared tumor in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)  
8.2 Store long-term at RT in sealed ECi-filled vials protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-pigment, lipid-rich tissues like melanoma, offering strong delipidation and depigmentation capacity while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with both Lectin (for functional perfused vasculature via intravascular labeling) and anti-CD31 immunostaining (for structural endothelial network), enabling direct spatial comparison. FDISCO maintains signal intensity of Alexa Fluor 488/647—critical for deep imaging in pigmented tumors—and achieves high refractive index matching (~1.52) suitable for light-sheet microscopy. Endogenous fluorescence is not relied upon, avoiding quenching issues.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Pre-labeling (assumes in vivo perfusion prior to fixation)  
1.1 Intracardiac perfusion with PBS followed by 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5–10 minutes per solution)  
1.2 Immediately after perfusion, inject 50 µg/mL Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* Isolectin B4) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in PBS into the circulation via left ventricle, allow 5 minutes circulation before PFA fixation to label only perfused vessels.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes circulation + immediate fixation)  

2 Post-fixation and Storage  
2.1 Post-fix tissue in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS overnight.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12–16 hours)  
2.2 Wash 3 × 1 hour in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
2.3 Store in PBS at 4 ℃ until processing (≤1 week).  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation and Depigmentation  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12–24 hours, protected from light)  

5 Rehydration (for immunostaining)  
5.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Permeabilization and Blocking  
6.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: 6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-CD31)  
7.1 Incubation with rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in antibody dilution buffer (3% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5–7 days, gentle shaking)  

8 Washing  
8.1 Wash 5 × 24 hours in washing buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Secondary Antibody Staining  
9.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 diluted 1:400 in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5–7 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

10 Final Washing  
10.1 Wash 5 × 24 hours in washing buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

11 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
11.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
12.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
12.3 Incubation with 100% ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.4 Final incubation in fresh 100% ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour, store at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-pigment, lipid-rich tissues like melanoma, offering strong delipidation and depigmentation capacity while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes. It effectively reduces melanin-induced light absorption/scattering and enables deep penetration of labeling reagents into dense tumor tissue (~10 mm). Lectin perfusion directly labels functional, perfused vasculature lumens, fulfilling the requirement to assess灌流 heterogeneity; CD31 immunostaining provides structural integrity of the entire endothelial network, enabling analysis of blind ends, abnormal branching, and vascular normalization. FDISCO is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, and supports robust antibody/dye penetration in thick, pigmented samples—critical for resolving core vs. periphery vascular architecture in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Depigmentation  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (CD31)  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBT + 5% normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 three more times, total of 4 washes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and DyLight 649-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin (10 μg/mL) in PBT + 5% normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, total of 3 washes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Bleaching (optional but recommended for melanin-rich tissue)  
10.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

11 Final Dehydration  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

13 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Store sample in fresh ECi at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
13.2 Mount sample in glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with ECi for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically optimized for high-pigment, lipid-rich tissues like melanoma, offering strong delipidation and effective melanin removal while preserving far-red fluorescence. It supports deep penetration of exogenous dyes/antibodies and is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 568 and 647—ideal for dual-channel structural (CD31) and functional perfusion (lectin) vascular labeling in red/far-red channels, minimizing autofluorescence and scattering from residual melanin. Lectin injected intravascularly labels only perfused vessels, enabling functional assessment, while CD31 immunostaining reveals the full endothelial network. FDISCO’s FP-preserving formulation is not needed here since endogenous FPs are absent; instead, its robust clearing power and compatibility with these dyes make it superior to aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC) that fail to remove melanin effectively.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Melanin and Heme Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody/dye labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody (1:200 in blocking buffer) and DyLight 649-conjugated or Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin (20 μg/mL in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma 112372-100G).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Final RI Matching and Storage  
11.1 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours before imaging; samples can be stored long-term in ECi at RT in the dark)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** The sample is a dense, fixed human breast cancer biopsy block (5 mm³), requiring strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration within 24–48 hours. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based method for dense clinical tissues, offering rapid clearing (<48 h), high refractive index matching, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated antibodies. Pan-Cytokeratin is a pan-epithelial marker that robustly labels residual epithelial carcinoma cells (including ductal and lobular subtypes) and is routinely used in surgical margin assessment. Hoechst 33342 provides nuclear counterstaining for tissue architecture and cell density context, enabling discrimination of tumor nests from stromal or necrotic regions. Although Hoechst requires caution in iDISCO+, short incubation in methanol-free conditions prior to dehydration preserves sufficient signal for structural reference without significant quenching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (pre-clearing)  
1.1 Rehydration: Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubation with PBST + 5% normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.2% sodium azide. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation with mouse anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., clone AE1/AE3, 1:200) in PBST + 5% NGS + 0.2% sodium azide. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Wash: Three washes with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
1.5 Secondary antibody incubation: Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBST + 5% NGS + 0.2% sodium azide. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Nuclear counterstain: Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (10 µg/mL) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Final wash: Two washes with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash: Two washes with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  

4 Rehydration (for RI matching transition)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in hexane. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer tissue to glass vial filled with fresh DBE for long-term storage at RT in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite until imaging)  
6.2 Mount cleared tissue in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires specific identification of residual epithelial cancer cells near surgical margins in dense, fixed human breast biopsy tissue. Pan-Cytokeratin is a well-validated, pan-epithelial marker that robustly labels carcinoma cells (including ductal and lobular subtypes) while excluding stromal and immune cells, fulfilling the requirement for a target-specific epithelial cancer cell marker. Alexa Fluor 647 is compatible with iDISCO+ and provides strong, photostable far-red signal ideal for deep imaging in cleared tissue. Hoechst 33342 serves as a nuclear counterstain to contextualize cellular morphology and spatial relationships but is not used as a primary cancer identifier. iDISCO+ was selected because it offers rapid, high-clearing power for dense clinical tissue blocks (~5 mm scale), enables deep antibody penetration via organic solvent-based delipidation, and completes within 24–48 hours—meeting the near-intraoperative timeframe. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on exogenous immunostaining. The method is established for human dense clinical specimens (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK) and provides sufficient morphological preservation for margin assessment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (reverse methanol series after storage/fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Pan-Cytokeratin primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes at 2-hour intervals)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution) and Hoechst 33342 (10 µg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

6 Post-staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
6.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Dehydration (methanol series)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

9 Re-dehydration  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Dichloromethane (DCM) Treatment  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh DBE for immediate light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging within 24 hours of RI matching)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The sample is a dense, fixed human breast cancer biopsy block (5 mm³), requiring rapid (<48 h), high-clearing-power processing with deep antibody penetration to resolve residual epithelial cancer nests near surgical margins. iDISCO+ is established for dense clinical tissues, provides strong delipidation and refractive index matching within 24–48 h, and supports robust immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor dyes. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on exogenous antibodies. Pan-Cytokeratin is a well-validated pan-epithelial tumor marker that specifically labels carcinoma cells (including ductal and lobular subtypes) in breast tissue, enabling unambiguous identification of residual cancer nests. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for morphological reference and distance measurement to cut surfaces, and while caution is noted for nuclear dyes in some contexts, DAPI remains compatible with iDISCO+ when used post-clearing or during rehydration and yields sufficient signal for margin assessment in small biopsies.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (reverse methanol series)  
1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Pan-Cytokeratin primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 10% NGS + 0.02% NaN₃).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  

6 Nuclear Counterstaining  
6.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Dehydration (methanol series)  
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.6 Repeat step 8.5 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Delipidation  
9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Repeat step 9.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE for storage and light-sheet/confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging; stable for ≥1 week)

**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 + Alexa Fluor 647, Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D visualization of prostate gland architecture with specific distinction between basal (p63+) and luminal/epithelial (Pan-Cytokeratin+) layers to assess basal cell loss—a key criterion in Gleason grading. p63 is a well-established nuclear marker for basal cells in prostate tissue, while Pan-Cytokeratin labels all epithelial cells, enabling clear delineation of adenocarcinoma-associated structural disruptions (e.g., fused glands, cribriform patterns). DAPI provides nuclear context without substituting for lineage identity. MACS is selected because it is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for dense human clinical biopsies (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), preserves antibody-based fluorescence (compatible with Alexa Fluor 488/647), enables deep penetration into 15-mm needle cores, and minimizes tissue distortion—critical for accurate morphometric analysis of gland topology. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), MACS avoids shrinkage and quenching risks while supporting multi-day antibody incubations needed for thick samples.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-p63 (1:200) and rabbit anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:300) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST to remove unbound secondary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) for nuclear counterstaining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer cleared tissue into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
3.2 Mount sample in a glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 to maintain RI matching during light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for imaging)
