**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (functional perfused vasculature), IB4 (functional perfused vasculature), CD31+Alexa Fluor 647 (structural endothelial reference)]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically validated for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like placenta (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier). It enables deep penetration of exogenous dyes/antibodies, preserves Alexa Fluor and lectin fluorescence better than iDISCO+/uDISCO, and achieves strong delipidation necessary for dense vascular networks in the labyrinth zone. Lectin and IB4 directly label the luminal surface of perfused vessels when administered pre-fixation or via post-fixation perfusion mimicry, allowing functional assessment of vascular patency; CD31 immunostaining provides structural context for total endothelial architecture. FDISCO’s compatibility with both lectins and Alexa Fluor 647 ensures dual-channel mapping of functional vs. structural vasculature in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Mimetic Vascular Labeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50 µg/mL DyLight 594-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin and 50 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4 in PBS containing 1% (wt/vol) BSA and 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

2 Immunostaining for Structural Endothelium  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1, 1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours × 4 changes)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours × 4 changes)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

5 Rehydration (for optional nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
5.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 (Optional) Incubation with TO-PRO-3 (1 µM) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.7 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

6 Dehydration (post-staining)  
6.1 Repeat steps 3.1–3.5 exactly as above.(Temperature: RT, Time: as specified per sub-step)  

7 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 2 changes)  
7.3 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, refractive index ~1.558).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage in dark)  
8.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional RI adjustment.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-DDX4 (VASA) + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-SYCP3 + Alexa Fluor 647, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration in dense, lipid-rich organs like the mouse testis (~8 mm scale), while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes and Alexa Fluor conjugates. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, enabling dual immunolabeling of germ cell populations (via DDX4/VASA, a conserved RNA helicase marking all germ cells from spermatogonia to spermatids) and meiotic prophase I spermatocytes (via SYCP3, a core component of the synaptonemal complex). Hoechst 33342 provides nuclear counterstaining to resolve seminiferous epithelium layering and nuclear morphology without interfering with target-specific signals. FDISCO outperforms aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS) in clearing speed and depth for this tissue tier and avoids the severe FP quenching seen in iDISCO+, while maintaining superior signal retention compared to uDISCO or PEGASOS for Alexa Fluor dyes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Immunolabeling (perform after rehydration if post-clearing labeling; however, for FDISCO, labeling is typically done pre-clearing—thus this step assumes labeling was completed prior to dehydration. If not, skip to RI matching. For completeness, include optional post-fixation stabilization.)  
3.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in PBS for stabilization (only if labeling was performed before dehydration).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Rehydration (if labeling was performed pre-clearing, this step is omitted; FDISCO protocol assumes labeling precedes dehydration. Proceed directly to RI matching.)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Nuclear Counterstaining (integrated during early dehydration if not done earlier; if omitted, perform here via diffusion in ECi-compatible dye)  
6.1 Incubation with 10 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in 80% (vol/vol) methanol/PBS (added during step 1.4 if pre-clearing; otherwise, add 10 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 directly to ECi for 1 hour).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Final Clearing and Mounting  
7.1 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, RI ≈ 1.597).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in sealed vial)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (from Dye_or_Fluorophore list) + CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample is a lipid- and hemoglobin-rich intact mouse placenta (~10 mm scale), requiring a high-clearing-power solvent-based method with deep probe penetration. uDISCO is established for T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tissues, provides strong delipidation and decolorization, and supports robust antibody/dye penetration. Unlike iDISCO+, uDISCO includes optimized dehydration and bleaching steps that enhance signal uniformity in dense, blood-rich tissues—addressing the user’s issue of weak central signal. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4) binds functional vascular lumens and complements CD31 (a pan-endothelial structural marker); both are compatible with uDISCO when conjugated to far-red fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 647, which resists quenching and enables deep imaging. Extended incubation ensures uniform labeling throughout the placental core.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (Hemoglobin/Endogenous Pigment Removal)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for Antibody/Dye Penetration)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary and Secondary Labeling (Combined Vascular Lumen + Endothelium)  
5.1 Incubation with mixture of:  
  - Biotinylated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin (10 µg/mL)  
  - Rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody (1:200 dilution)  
  in PBST + 5% NDS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
5.3 Incubation with mixture of:  
  - Streptavidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500)  
  - Donkey anti-rat IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500)  
  in PBST + 5% NDS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.4 Wash with PBST (4 changes, 2 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours total)  

6 Dehydration (Post-Labeling)  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation  
7.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, RI ≈ 1.596).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.4 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial with fresh ECi and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)  
9.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional washing.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [SYCP3 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense, lipid-rich soft organs like the mouse testis (~8 mm scale), enabling deep antibody penetration while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes and Alexa Fluor conjugates. It is compatible with nuclear counterstains (DAPI) and lectin-based vasculature/structure labeling, and crucially supports robust immunolabeling of intracellular meiotic markers such as SYCP3—a specific marker for synaptonemal complexes in pachytene/diplotene spermatocytes—allowing precise identification of meiotic-stage germ cells within intact seminiferous tubules. Lectin (IB4) labels Sertoli cell boundaries and tubule architecture, providing spatial context for germ cell layering. FDISCO avoids the severe quenching seen in iDISCO+ for far-red dyes and offers better structural preservation than uDISCO for delicate tubular morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if pigmentation observed)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-SYCP3 primary antibody (e.g., rabbit anti-SYCP3, 1:200) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat washing with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Repeat washing with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Final wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: overnight)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) + Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated IB4 lectin (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Repeat washing with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Repeat incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Transfer to fresh ECi for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [SYCP3 + Alexa Fluor 568, DDX4/VASA + Alexa Fluor 647, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like intact mouse testes (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier). It preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes and Hoechst far better than iDISCO+, which likely caused signal loss and structural damage in the user’s prior attempt due to excessive decolorization at RT. FDISCO uses controlled temperature shifts and avoids prolonged harsh oxidation, thereby preserving delicate seminiferous tubule architecture and germ cell adhesion. The chosen markers—SYCP3 (a core component of the meiotic synaptonemal complex) and DDX4/VASA (a germ cell-specific RNA helicase)—are well-established, target-specific antibodies compatible with organic-solvent protocols when paired with Alexa Fluor conjugates. Hoechst provides nuclear counterstaining without significant quenching in FDISCO and enables visualization of layered spermatogenic nuclei within tubules. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 568, Alexa Fluor 647, Hoechst) are explicitly compatible with FDISCO per the knowledge base.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Decolorization  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) saponin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-SYCP3 (1:200) and anti-DDX4/VASA (1:200) in PBST + 5% donkey serum + 0.5% saponin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.5% saponin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Repeat washing step 6.1 two more times with fresh buffer each time.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) in PBST + 5% donkey serum + 0.5% saponin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.5% saponin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
8.2 Repeat washing step 8.1 two more times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (10 µg/mL) in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Final Dehydration  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Incubation with hexane (anhydrous, ≥99%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.4 Incubation with fresh hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.5 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, RI ≈ 1.557).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
12.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [SYCP3 + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense, lipid-rich tissues like the mouse testis (~8 mm scale), enabling deep penetration of antibodies and dyes while preserving fluorescence of synthetic fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series, DAPI). It is established for T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM and compatible with all selected labels. SYCP3 is a meiosis-specific marker that labels synaptonemal complexes in spermatocytes, allowing precise spatial mapping of meiotic stages within seminiferous tubules. Lectin (IB4) binds to glycocalyx on Sertoli and germ cell surfaces, outlining tubule architecture and lumen boundaries. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining to resolve layered organization of spermatogonia (basal), spermatocytes (middle), and spermatids/sperm (luminal), enabling stage identification based on nuclear morphology and position. This combination fulfills the requirement for target-specific labeling (SYCP3 for meiotic cells, IB4 for tubule structure) plus nuclear context (DAPI) without relying on endogenous fluorescent proteins.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if pigmentation present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-SYCP3 primary antibody (1:200 in staining buffer: PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% DMSO + 5% normal donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4 lectin (10 µg/mL) in staining buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation and Clearing  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

13.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
13.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Hu C/D + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The target structures—myenteric and submucosal plexuses—require specific neuronal markers that label both neuronal somata (Hu C/D) and pan-neuronal fibers (PGP9.5). uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for long tubular organs (T06 tier), offering high clearing power, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488/647 dyes. It achieves high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging of intact 6 cm colon segments while preserving 3D topology despite moderate tissue shrinkage, which is acceptable for network connectivity analysis. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are avoided per protocol constraints; instead, robust immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor conjugates ensures signal stability through dehydration and organic solvent steps.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Hu C/D (1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol: 2 changes, 30 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-bleach nuclear counterstain; omitted here per restriction)  
*(Skipped – no nuclear stain used as primary neural markers suffice)*  

5 Dehydration (post-bleach)  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage or immediate imaging)  
7.2 Mount in custom DBE-compatible chamber for light-sheet microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for imaging)

HuC/D and PGP9.5 are well-validated pan-neuronal markers for enteric neuron somata and fibers; dual labeling ensures robust detection of both cell bodies (HuC/D) and axonal processes (PGP9.5). Phalloidin labels F-actin in smooth muscle layers, aiding anatomical registration of neural plexus positions relative to circular/longitudinal muscle. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568/647) are compatible with uDISCO per compatibility data.

1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: anti-HuC/D (1:500), anti-PGP9.5 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Repeat wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies and Phalloidin in blocking buffer: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 568–Phalloidin (1:200).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

6 Post-staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 90% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Hu C/D + Alexa Fluor 488, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for long, dense tubular tissues like the mouse colon (T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM tier). It provides strong delipidation and deep antibody/dye penetration required for full-thickness labeling of both myenteric and submucosal plexuses. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in iDISCO+, so we use immunostaining with Alexa Fluor dyes, which are compatible. Hu C/D (also known as PGP9.5) is a well-validated pan-neuronal marker specific for enteric neurons and fibers, enabling clear visualization of both plexuses. Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 robustly labels F-actin in smooth muscle layers (circular and longitudinal), providing structural reference to determine the spatial relationship between neural networks and gut wall layers. This combination satisfies the scientific goal of mapping 3D topological correspondence between enteric nervous system and muscular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

5.1 Incubation with anti-Hu C/D (e.g., Invitrogen A-21271 or equivalent) diluted 1:500 in blocking solution + 1 U/mL Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 568.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)

8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)

9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-RBPMS + Alexa Fluor 488, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The problem requires high-clearing power for intact, pigment-rich mouse eyeballs (~3–4 mm) while preserving 3D spatial relationships between retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and superficial vasculature. iDISCO+ is an established organic solvent-based method for whole-eye clearing with strong delipidation and deep antibody/dye penetration, suitable for dense ocular tissues. Endogenous fluorescence is not required; thus, quenching by iDISCO+ is acceptable. RBPMS is a highly specific cytoplasmic marker for RGCs, superior to nuclear stains or non-specific markers. IB4 (isolectin B4 from Griffonia simplicifolia) binds specifically to endothelial glycocalyx in murine retinal vasculature and is compatible with iDISCO+ when conjugated to stable fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 568. Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 are both iDISCO+-compatible and provide spectrally distinct channels for dual-channel 3D imaging of RGCs and vessels.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for pigmented eyes)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-RBPMS + Alexa Fluor 488, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The intact mouse eyeball is a dense, pigmented, and lipid-rich tissue (T12 tier) requiring strong delipidation and high clearing power for deep imaging of retinal layers. iDISCO+ provides rapid, effective organic solvent–based clearing with excellent penetration for antibody/dye labeling, which is essential given the presence of RPE melanin and the need to image through the entire globe. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are not required; instead, we use target-specific immunolabeling: RBPMS is a well-validated, selective marker for retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), and IB4 (Isolectin B4) robustly labels the luminal surface of retinal vasculature without requiring transgenic models. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 are compatible with iDISCO+ and resist quenching during dehydration and delipidation. This combination enables simultaneous high-contrast visualization of RGC somata and vascular networks in 3D within the intact eye.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for RPE pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with anti-RBPMS primary antibody (e.g., 1:200 in blocking solution) and IB4 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (e.g., 1:100 in blocking solution).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat washing step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody Labeling (if needed; skip if using directly conjugated primary)  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400 in blocking solution).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-labeling Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging  
12.1 Store samples immersed in DBE in glass vials protected from light at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-Brn3a (POU4F1) + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-RBPMS + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires dual-specific labeling of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) via both a canonical transcription factor (Brn3a/POU4F1) and a cytoplasmic RGC identity marker (RBPMS) to cross-validate cell identity, reduce false positives/negatives, and enable 3D colocalization analysis in intact mouse eyes. iDISCO+ is selected because it provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration in dense, pigmented tissues like the whole eye—critical for uniform labeling across the entire retina without dissection. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses robust, covalently conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes (488 and 568), which are fully compatible with iDISCO+ and offer high signal-to-noise. Nuclear dyes (e.g., DAPI) are excluded as primary markers per problem constraints but may be optionally added post-clearing for laminar reference if needed.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for pigment-rich tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Brn3a (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:200–1:500) and anti-RBPMS (goat or rabbit polyclonal, 1:200–1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Washes Post Primary  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host IgG (for Brn3a) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-host IgG (for RBPMS), each at 1:500 dilution in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation, protected from light)  

8 Washes Post Secondary  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each, protected from light)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial suitable for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour until imaging)  

12 Imaging Preparation

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [RBPMS + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The problem requires strong pigment removal (especially RPE melanin), deep penetration into dense intact mouse eyeballs (~3–4 mm), and simultaneous high-fidelity labeling of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and vascular structures. iDISCO+ is an organic solvent–based method with high clearing power, effective delipidation, and robust melanin bleaching—critical for overcoming RPE-induced background and light absorption. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, the user’s goal does not rely on them; instead, we use target-specific primary antibodies (RBPMS for RGCs, CD31 for endothelial cells) and lectin IB4 (binds endothelial glycocalyx) conjugated to photostable, iDISCO+-compatible Alexa Fluor dyes. This combination ensures specific, dual-channel detection of RGC somata and vascular lumen/network with minimal background, enabling precise 3D spatial correlation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (RPE pigment removal)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-RBPMS (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:200), Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:200), and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a rapid, high-clearing-power solvent-based method compatible with small (1–3 mm) fixed human brain organoids, enabling deep penetration of antibodies and dyes while preserving 3D morphology with minimal distortion relative to other solvent methods. It is explicitly compatible with DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647—critical for our labeling strategy. Ki67 (MKI67) is the gold-standard marker for proliferating nuclei, directly addressing the need to map spatial proliferation changes under drug treatment. Phalloidin labels F-actin to reveal overall organoid architecture, cortical layering, and structural integrity (e.g., fragmentation or collapse). DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for total cell density and organoid volume quantification. This combination enables simultaneous assessment of growth (via volume and F-actin structure), cellularity (DAPI), and proliferation suppression (Ki67 loss)—all essential for high-throughput drug toxicity screening.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling and Cytoskeletal Staining  
2.1 Rehydration: stepwise rehydration through 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
2.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-Ki67 (1:200 in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% serum).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Wash: 5 × 1 hour washes with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
2.5 Secondary antibody + Phalloidin + DAPI co-staining: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse/rabbit IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin (1:100), DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Wash: 5 × 1 hour washes with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Wash: 2 × 1 hour with 100% methanol at RT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer organoids into glass vials filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage)  
6.2 Equilibrate samples in ECi for at least 1 hour before light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, Keratin 14 (K14) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The clinical human skin biopsy is a dense, lipid-rich tissue requiring strong clearing with minimal morphological distortion to accurately quantify epidermal nerve fiber (IENF) architecture. MACS is an aqueous-based method established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK samples, offering excellent antibody penetration, preservation of fine neurite morphology, and compatibility with both Alexa Fluor 488 (for PGP9.5, a gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for IENF in clinical diagnostics) and Alexa Fluor 647 (for K14 to delineate epidermal boundaries). Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., uDISCO/iDISCO+), MACS avoids significant tissue shrinkage and preserves 3D geometry critical for IENF density and branching analysis. Endogenous fluorescence is not relied upon; instead, robust immunolabeling ensures specific, high-contrast visualization of IENFs from dermal-epidermal junction into suprabasal layers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (performed on fixed, non-cleared tissue)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and rabbit anti-Keratin 14 (1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation, protected from light)  
1.5 Washing with PBST three times, 1 hour each, followed by one overnight wash in PBS at 4 ℃.(Temperature: RT for first three washes, then 4 ℃ for overnight, Time: 1 hour ×3 + 12 hours)  

2 Dehydration (optional pre-clearing step for aqueous methods; omitted for MACS as it is fully aqueous-compatible)  

3 Tissue Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15 wt/vol% sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30 wt/vol% sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50 wt/vol% sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate imaging or long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark.(Temperature: 4 ℃ for storage, RT for imaging, Time: indefinite storage possible)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67 + Alexa Fluor 488, PCNA + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for rapid, high-clearing-power processing of small (1–3 mm) dense tissues like brain organoids, with excellent preservation of exogenous dye fluorescence (including Alexa Fluor dyes and DAPI). It avoids the structural fragility seen in aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC) by using controlled dehydration and delipidation that minimizes swelling-induced fragmentation. FDISCO is compatible with both Ki67 and PCNA immunolabeling—two complementary proliferation markers—and retains strong nuclear DAPI signal for volumetric segmentation and spatial mapping of proliferating cells. Its speed (<2 days total) and compatibility with high-throughput screening make it ideal for drug toxicity assays requiring minimal morphological distortion and robust dual-proliferation readouts.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (post-PFA fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Ki67 (1:200) and anti-PCNA (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.02% NaN₃ in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

6 Post-staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  
6.2 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Nuclear Counterstaining  
7.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
7.2 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Dehydration  
8.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 2 times)  

9 Delipidation and Bleaching  
9.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

10 Re-equilibration in Methanol  
10.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging  
12.1 Transfer organoids into glass vials filled with fresh ECi and store at RT in the dark until imaging (stable for ≥1 week)  
12.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DAPI (405 nm), Alexa Fluor 488 (488 nm), and Alexa Fluor 568 (561 nm)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67 + Alexa Fluor 488, PCNA + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense tissues like brain organoids (1–3 mm), enabling deep antibody penetration and excellent preservation of Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with both Ki67 and PCNA immunostaining—two canonical nuclear markers for cell cycle progression (Ki67: all active phases except G0; PCNA: S-phase DNA replication)—and preserves DAPI signal for total nuclear segmentation. Unlike iDISCO+, FDISCO maintains robust fluorescence of Alexa Fluor conjugates and small-molecule dyes without quenching, critical for quantitative 3D comparison of proliferation zones. Its relatively fast protocol aligns with high-throughput screening needs, and minimal morphological distortion ensures accurate spatial analysis of outer proliferative layers versus central quiescent regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and 0.3 M glycine in PBS to reduce autofluorescence and enhance antibody access.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Ki67 (1:200) and anti-PCNA (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (5% donkey serum, 0.2% Tween-20, 0.02% NaN₃ in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  

5 Post-Staining Washes  
5.1 Wash with PBST three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
5.2 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) for nuclear counterstain.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Final wash with PBS twice.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Bleaching (Optional but Recommended for Organoids)  
7.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Rehydration (for FDISCO-specific RI Matching Transition)  
8.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with FDISCO-RI solution (88% (wt/wt) iodixanol in distilled water, adjusted to pH 7.4 with NaOH).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Transfer to fresh FDISCO-RI solution for final clearing.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Store samples in FDISCO-RI solution at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite for short-term; up to 2 weeks recommended)  
10.2 Mount cleared organoids in glass-bottom imaging chambers filled with FDISCO-RI for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry/RFP]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically validated for small whole organisms like C. elegans and preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and mCherry/RFP) without quenching. It maintains fine neuronal morphology—critical for resolving the neural ring, neurites, and nerve bundles—while providing sufficient refractive index matching for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., confocal or light-sheet microscopy). Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), Ce3D avoids organic solvents that degrade FP signals. Among aqueous methods compatible with C. elegans (MACS, CUBIC, ScaleS, SeeDB2, Ce3D), Ce3D offers superior structural preservation and has been explicitly optimized for nematode tissue, minimizing distortion of the ~1 mm adult worm while enabling deep imaging of internal neural architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Repeat wash with fresh PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Ce3D Clearing Solution Preparation and Incubation  
2.1 Prepare Ce3D clearing solution: 45% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in distilled water. Filter sterilize (0.22 μm).  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D clearing solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Transfer samples to fresh Ce3D solution for final RI equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

4 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Mount individual worms in glass-bottom imaging dishes or capillaries using fresh Ce3D solution as immersion medium. Avoid air bubbles. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (from DyLight 594-conjugated *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4) or biotinylated IB4 + streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** The clinical human skin biopsy is dense and lipid-rich, requiring a clearing method with strong penetration yet minimal morphological distortion to preserve the fine architecture of epidermal nerve fibers and dermal papillae. MACS is an aqueous-based method established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK samples, offering excellent antibody/dye penetration, compatibility with both Alexa Fluor dyes and lectin/IB4 labeling, and preservation of tissue geometry—critical for quantitative spatial analysis of IENF density and vascular relationships. PGP9.5 is the gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for IENF in clinical skin biopsies, while IB4/Lectin robustly labels endothelial glycocalyx in human dermal microvasculature without cross-reactivity with nerves. MACS preserves fluorescence intensity of Alexa Fluor 488/594 and supports long-term storage, enabling high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage (Assume pre-fixation; if not, perform first)  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS, pH 7.4. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.3 Store in PBS with 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide at 4 ℃ until processing (≤1 week).  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (IENF labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody: mouse anti-human PGP9.5 (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

4 Washing Post Primary  
4.1 Wash with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Lectin/IB4 Co-staining (Vascular + Neural labeling)  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300) + DyLight 594-conjugated *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4 (10 µg/mL) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
*(Alternative: if using biotinylated IB4, use 10 µg/mL biotin-IB4 + 1:300 streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 594 in same step)*  

6 Washing Post Staining  
6.1 Wash with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

7 Dehydration (Optional but recommended for MACS compatibility)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Rehydration (for aqueous clearing compatibility)  
8.1 Reverse methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
8.2 Final wash in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Optical Clearing with MACS  
9.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

10 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
10.1 Transfer sample to fresh MACS-R2 in glass-bottom imaging dish or chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
10.2 Seal with coverslip using VALAP or silicone grease to prevent evaporation during imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at 4 ℃ for ≤1 month)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically validated for small whole organisms like C. elegans and preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and mCherry) without quenching. It maintains fine neuronal morphology in the nerve ring and ventral nerve cord while enabling deep imaging with minimal distortion—critical for comparing spatial relationships between two genetically encoded fluorophores. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), Ce3D avoids organic solvents that degrade or bleach FP signals. Among aqueous methods compatible with T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM, Ce3D offers superior structural preservation over CUBIC/ScaleS and better dye penetration than SeeDB2/TDE, making it optimal for high-resolution 3D mapping of dual-color neuronal projections in fixed C. elegans.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 1× PBS (pH 7.4) to ensure complete fixation prior to clearing.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, repeat ×3)  

3 Permeabilization and Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-P solution (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 1× PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Optical Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-C1 reagent (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-C2 reagent (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C3 reagent (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-M reagent (87% (wt/vol) fructose, 33% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in distilled water; final RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer cleared worm into a glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary tube filled with fresh Ce3D-M reagent.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry/RFP]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically validated for small whole organisms like C. elegans (tier T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM). It preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and mCherry/RFP) without quenching, maintains native morphology with minimal distortion or shrinkage, and allows sufficient reagent penetration for optional counterstaining if needed. Given that the scientific goal relies on dual-color endogenous reporters to map neural architecture—including the nerve ring, head neuron somata, neurites, and ventral nerve cord—no additional immunostaining is required. However, Ce3D remains compatible with nuclear dyes (e.g., DAPI/Hoechst) should future experiments require cellular context; for this protocol, only intrinsic EGFP and mCherry/RFP signals are used as primary markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to ensure consistent fixation across samples.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS three times to remove residual PFA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes per wash)  

2 Dehydration (Optional Pre-Clearing Equilibration)  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS to begin refractive index pre-equilibration and reduce osmotic shock.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Ce3D Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent A (8 M urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH adjusted to 7.5 with NaOH).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D Reagent A for a second round to ensure complete lipid solubilization and tissue homogenization.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Transfer samples to Ce3D Reagent B (86% (wt/wt) iodixanol, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, final RI ≈ 1.45–1.47).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh Ce3D Reagent B for final RI equilibration and fluorescence stabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer cleared worms into glass-bottom imaging dishes or capillary tubes filled with Ce3D Reagent B to maintain RI matching during acquisition.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 2 weeks)
