**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** Human skin biopsies are lipid- and pigment-rich (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH), requiring a high-clearing-power solvent-based method. FDISCO provides strong delipidation and melanin quenching while preserving Alexa Fluor dyes—critical for overcoming weak IENF signal and melanin-induced background. PGP9.5 is the gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for IENF in clinical diagnostics; CD31 robustly labels endothelial cells of the superficial dermal vasculature, providing spatial reference without cross-reactivity. FDISCO is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, enables deep antibody penetration into dense epidermis, and minimizes fluorescence quenching compared to iDISCO+. Its organic solvent sequence effectively reduces melanin absorption while maintaining tissue geometry better than uDISCO for small biopsies.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (perform before clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-CD31 (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 5 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 5 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Melanin Quenching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration (reverse methanol series)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Organic Solvent Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM), second change.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma E101-100G-F).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
6.2 Mount in ECi-filled chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy with RI ≈ 1.558.

It minimizes tissue distortion, maintains fine neural structures such as the ~10–20 μm-wide nerve ring, and achieves refractive index (RI) matching suitable for high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging within 1–2 days. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), Ce3D avoids organic solvents that denature fluorescent proteins. Among aqueous methods compatible with T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM, Ce3D provides superior antibody/dye penetration if future immunostaining is needed, though here we rely solely on genetically encoded reporters as required.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT) to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Repeat wash with fresh PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Ce3D Clearing Solution Preparation and Incubation  
2.1 Prepare Ce3D clearing solution: 10% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (NMN), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, in distilled water, pH adjusted to 8.5 with NaOH.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A – prepare fresh)  
2.2 Incubate samples in Ce3D clearing solution with gentle agitation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Transfer cleared worms to Ce3D RI-matching solution: 60% (wt/vol) iodixanol (OptiPrep™) in PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Optional: Replace with fresh Ce3D RI-matching solution for optimal clarity.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer individual worms into glass-bottom imaging chambers or agarose-coated dishes using a transfer pipette.  
4.2 Cover samples completely with Ce3D RI-matching solution to prevent dehydration and maintain optical homogeneity.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based high-clearing-power method established for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like human skin biopsies (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH). It enables deep antibody penetration into dense dermal matrix while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes and Hoechst—critical for simultaneous IENF (via PGP9.5), superficial vascular network (via CD31), and epidermal nuclear stratification (via Hoechst). Unlike iDISCO+, FDISCO maintains superior signal stability for far-red and red fluorophores and shows compatibility with nuclear counterstains, allowing accurate epidermal thickness and layer reference without distortion-induced counting bias. The method’s rapid clearing kinetics suit small (3–4 mm) biopsy cores, and its final high-refractive-index (RI ≈ 1.56) DBE-based mounting enables high-resolution light-sheet or confocal imaging of the full epidermal–dermal junction in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash fixed skin biopsy (3–4 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick, 4% PFA-fixed) 3× with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash)  
1.2 Block in blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for permeabilization and non-specific binding reduction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-CD31/PECAM1 (1:200) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash 5× with PBST to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse/rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rat/mouse IgG (1:500), plus Hoechst 33342 (10 µg/mL), all in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours in dark)  
1.6 Wash 5× with PBST to remove unbound secondaries and excess Hoechst. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours in dark)  
3.2 Wash 2× with 100% methanol to remove residual H₂O₂. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash)  

4 Rehydration (optional intermediate step for dye stability; omitted in standard FDISCO but included here to protect Hoechst)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish (1–5 mm) that preserves fine cellular morphology with minimal distortion—critical for analyzing hair cell architecture and stereocilia bundle geometry. It supports deep penetration of both phalloidin and antibodies while maintaining fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles with high specificity, and Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, target-specific marker for zebrafish lateral line hair cells. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial context without interfering with hair cell labeling. Ce3D’s compatibility with these fluorophores and its gentle handling of delicate epithelial structures make it optimal for this developmental imaging goal.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling and Phalloidin Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS), 5 changes over 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500 in blocking solution) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 5 changes over 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) for nuclear counterstain. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS, 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C (75% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Equilibration in final RI-matching solution: Ce3D-C (same as 2.3) until sample becomes optically transparent (typically complete after step 2.3). (Temperature: RT, Time: 0 hours additional—proceed directly to imaging)  
3.2 Mounting in glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary using fresh Ce3D-C as immersion medium. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish (1–5 mm), preserving fine cellular morphology with minimal distortion—critical for assessing stereociliary bundle integrity and orientation. It supports deep penetration of both small-molecule dyes (e.g., Phalloidin) and antibodies, and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 488/568 fluorophores. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia without requiring antibody amplification, while Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, specific marker for zebrafish lateral line hair cells, enabling unambiguous identification of the target population.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (for Myosin VIIa)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody diluted 1:200 in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated secondary antibody (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Tissue Clearing with Ce3D  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-M (80% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish and submerge in fresh Ce3D-M (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)–Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish samples (1–5 mm), preserving endogenous fluorescence and supporting deep penetration of both phalloidin and antibodies. It minimizes tissue distortion—critical for accurate 3D spatial analysis of neuromast architecture. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in hair cell stereocilia bundles with high specificity, while β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a well-validated marker for peripheral neuronal processes, including lateral line nerves in zebrafish. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 are fully compatible with Ce3D and provide spectrally separable signals for dual-channel imaging of hair cells and innervating neurites.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (for lateral line nerve fibers)  
2.1 Incubation with mouse anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) antibody diluted 1:500 in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
3.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 4 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash, protected from light)  

4 Tissue Clearing with Ce3D  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-M solution (80% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; final RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
5.2 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish and submerge in fresh Ce3D-M for immediate light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: imaging within 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP/YFP (endogenous reporter), SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is an aqueous, plant-optimized clearing method specifically validated for *Arabidopsis* whole seedlings. It preserves endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence without quenching, minimizes tissue distortion, and is compatible with cell wall dyes. SCRI Renaissance 2200 is a far-red fluorescent dye that selectively labels plant cell walls with high contrast, minimal cytoplasmic background, and excellent compatibility with GFP/YFP imaging. This combination enables simultaneous visualization of transgenic fluorescence and precise cellular/tissue architecture in both root and shoot without requiring antibody-based labeling.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Cell Wall Staining  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1% (wt/vol) SCRI Renaissance 2200 in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with distilled water (3 changes, 30 minutes each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (10% (wt/vol) KSCN, 12% (wt/vol) glycerol, 8% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Replace with fresh ClearSee solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Transfer sample to fresh ClearSee solution in glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour prior to imaging)  
3.2 Seal sample under coverslip with ClearSee as mounting medium; store at 4 ℃ if not imaged immediately (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 week)

**Justification:** ClearSee is an aqueous-based, plant-optimized optical clearing method specifically validated for intact *Arabidopsis thaliana* seedlings. SCRI Renaissance 2200 is a cell wall-selective fluorogenic dye compatible with ClearSee that labels cellulose-rich structures without requiring antibodies, enabling precise delineation of tissue boundaries and cellular layers alongside fluorescent protein signals. This combination meets the requirement to retain intrinsic fluorescence while providing structural context at whole-seedling scale.

2.1 Incubation with 10 µM SCRI Renaissance 2200 in distilled water (prepared fresh from DMSO stock; final DMSO ≤0.1%) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
2.2 Wash with distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes, protected from light)

3.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (10% (wt/vol) xylitol, 10% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24–48 hours, gentle shaking)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor 488, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish samples (1–5 mm), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal swelling or shrinkage—addressing the user’s issue of severe expansion in ScaleS. It supports deep penetration of both antibodies and phalloidin conjugates while preserving fluorescence intensity of Alexa Fluor dyes. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, specific marker for zebrafish lateral line hair cells, and direct labeling with Alexa Fluor–conjugated phalloidin robustly visualizes F-actin–rich stereociliary bundles without requiring genetic reporters. This dual-labeling strategy avoids reliance on endogenous fluorescent proteins (which may be weak or absent) and ensures strong, stable signal retention through Ce3D processing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining and Phalloidin Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 1% DMSO, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against Myosin VIIa (1:200 dilution in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes at 2-hour intervals)  
1.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-host secondary antibody (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes at 2-hour intervals)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Equilibration in final RI-matching solution Ce3D-M (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 33% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0; RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer to glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary tube and submerge completely in fresh Ce3D-M for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** TDE  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP/YFP (内源), SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** TDE is an aqueous, refractive index–tunable clearing method established for whole Arabidopsis seedlings (T11_PLANT_WHOLE_SEEDLING) that preserves endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence without quenching, unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). It effectively reduces light scattering while allowing sufficient penetration of cell wall dyes like SCRI Renaissance 2200—a validated fluorescent probe for plant cell walls that binds cellulose and is compatible with FP imaging. TDE also enables gradual RI matching to minimize tissue distortion, critical for accurate 3D localization of root and vascular signals. The prior use of ClearSee likely failed due to insufficient delipidation/pigment removal; TDE’s higher RI tunability and compatibility with mild pre-clearing steps improve chlorophyll clearance and transparency in pigmented tissues like cotyledons.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-Clearing Chlorophyll Removal  
1.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol aqueous solution to remove residual chlorophyll.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 90% (vol/vol) ethanol aqueous solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Rehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 90% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.4 Incubation with distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Cell Wall Staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200  
3.1 Incubation with 0.1 mg/mL SCRI Renaissance 2200 in distilled water (filter-sterilized).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

4 TDE-Based Optical Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 30% (wt/vol) TDE (2,2′-thiodiethanol, Sigma-Aldrich 167179) in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% (wt/vol) TDE in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 70% (wt/vol) TDE in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 85% (wt/vol) TDE in distilled water (final RI ≈ 1.45–1.47, optimal for confocal/light-sheet imaging of Arabidopsis).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours or until fully transparent)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount sample in 85% (wt/vol) TDE solution in glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary tube, avoiding bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense mouse soft tissues (5–20 mm), offering strong delipidation and deep dye/antibody penetration—critical for visualizing NMJs throughout the entire ~8 mm腓肠肌. It preserves fine structural integrity of AChR clusters and axonal processes while enabling high-resolution 3D imaging. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in iDISCO+, so direct labeling with stable synthetic fluorophores is required. α-Bungarotoxin specifically and irreversibly binds postsynaptic AChRs, making it the gold-standard probe for NMJ postsynaptic labeling. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a well-validated marker for neuronal microtubules in motor axons and nerve terminals, allowing precise delineation of presynaptic architecture. Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 are both highly compatible with iDISCO+ and provide spectrally distinct, photostable signals for dual-channel NMJ analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (for motor nerve terminals)  
2.1 Incubation with rabbit anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) antibody diluted 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer (5% NDS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

3 Secondary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 diluted 1:400 in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

4 α-Bungarotoxin Labeling (for AChR clusters)  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated α-bungarotoxin (1 µg/mL) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
4.2 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Bleaching (optional, if tissue pigmentation present)  
6.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) in methanol (prepared fresh: 1 part 30% H₂O₂ + 5 parts methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
6.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Delipidation  
7.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong lipid removal and high refractive index matching in dense tissues like skeletal muscle, while preserving exogenous fluorescent dyes such as Alexa Fluor conjugates—critical given the user’s prior issue with weak alpha-bungarotoxin signal after THF/DBE. Unlike iDISCO+, FDISCO explicitly preserves Alexa Fluor 488/568/647 signals and minimizes fluorescence quenching. The method supports deep penetration of antibodies and small-molecule probes into intact ~8 mm muscles. For labeling: alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically binds acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) at the postsynaptic membrane without requiring permeabilization steps that risk morphology; TUJ1 (anti-β-III Tubulin) robustly labels motor axons and nerve terminals in NMJs and is compatible with organic solvent protocols when applied before dehydration. Both are paired with Alexa Fluor dyes known to be FDISCO-compatible per the knowledge base.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for gentle rehydration and membrane permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS three times, 30 minutes each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (for motor neuron axons)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:500 in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Alpha-Bungarotoxin Co-Staining  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (1 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 four times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Transfer to fresh 100% ECi for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for dense soft tissues like skeletal muscle, offering high refractive index matching, strong delipidation power, and excellent preservation of dye-based fluorescence—including Alexa Fluor 647 and 488—while minimizing signal quenching. It is established for mouse soft organs in the 5–20 mm size range and provides rapid, deep penetration suitable for thick (~3 mm) intact gastrocnemius. Alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically labels acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) at the postsynaptic membrane without requiring antibodies, fulfilling the requirement to avoid substitution. TUJ1 (β-III Tubulin) is a well-validated marker for motor neuron axons and nerve terminals, enabling co-visualization of presynaptic elements to contextualize NMJ architecture. FDISCO’s compatibility with both fluorophores ensures robust signal retention for quantitative analysis of AChR cluster morphology, fragmentation, and spatial distribution along muscle fibers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ added to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (wt/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary and Secondary Labeling (if applicable) – *Note: alpha-bungarotoxin is direct; TUJ1 requires primary + secondary*  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:500 in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 2% (wt/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
5.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG secondary antibody diluted 1:500 in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 2% (wt/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

6 Direct Postsynaptic Labeling with alpha-bungarotoxin  
6.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (1 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

7 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Store sample immersed in ethyl cinnamate (ECi) in a sealed glass vial protected from light at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
9.2 Mount sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with ethyl cinnamate for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of the entire gastric wall pan-neuronal network—including fine nerve terminals—across a thick (~8 mm), multi-layered organ. PGP9.5 and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) are well-established pan-neuronal markers that robustly label both myelinated and unmyelinated fibers, including vagal efferents/afferents in the gut, satisfying the requirement for comprehensive neural labeling beyond pathway-specific tracers. uDISCO is selected because it provides strong delipidation and high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.52) ideal for large, dense soft organs like the mouse stomach, enables deep antibody penetration, and preserves fine neurite morphology with minimal scattering. Although uDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling relies on exogenous Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondary antibodies, which are fully compatible and exhibit excellent signal retention in uDISCO. The method’s speed (days vs. weeks) and compatibility with dual-color far-red/green imaging make it optimal for comparative regional analysis across gastric subdomains.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction in gastric tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 part 30% H₂O₂ + 5 parts methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:1000).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Repeat wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (anti-rabbit, 1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-mouse, 1:500) in blocking buffer + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  

8 Post-Labeling Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Repeat wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)

12.1 Transfer cleared stomach to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, uniform labeling of the entire gastric neural plexus across all wall layers in a relatively large (~20 mm), dense soft organ. PGP9.5 and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) are well-established pan-neuronal markers that robustly label enteric and vagal nerve fibers in the gastrointestinal tract. Dual immunolabeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes enables comprehensive 3D mapping of nerve density, branching, and regional distribution. iDISCO+ is selected because it provides strong delipidation and high clearing power for dense mouse soft organs of this size tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), supports deep antibody penetration via methanol-based permeabilization, and is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488/568/647 conjugates. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on exogenous immunostaining. Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 568) is included as an auxiliary channel to delineate smooth muscle architecture, aiding layer-specific nerve localization. Nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) are omitted due to poor compatibility and lack of structural utility for neural network analysis in thick cleared tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented tissue; include if sample shows discoloration)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:200) and anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) and anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400), plus Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200), all diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Mount cleared stomach in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with DBE, orienting desired gastric region (e.g., corpus vs. antrum) for optimal light-sheet or confocal acquisition.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 month)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源)]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP and tdTomato fluorescence to trace two distinct projection neuron populations across long-range circuits in the intact adult mouse brain. Solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) typically quench or severely attenuate endogenous fluorescent proteins, despite some variants claiming FP compatibility. Among aqueous clearing methods established for whole adult mouse brains (T04 tier), MACS offers strong delipidation and refractive index homogenization while fully preserving EGFP and tdTomato signals, as confirmed by compatibility data. It also supports deep tissue penetration without significant distortion, enabling accurate 3D reconstruction of axonal trajectories and spatial overlap analysis in the amygdala–PFC–thalamus–NAc network. No additional immunolabeling is needed since the genetic reporters already label the target projection neurons and their axons.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation; skip if directly in PBS)  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Clearing (Delipidation and Initial RI Matching)  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 solution (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 36 hours)  

3 Intermediate RI Matching  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R1 solution (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Final RI Matching and Fluorescence Stabilization  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R2 solution (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer cleared brain into fresh MACS-R2 in a light-protected imaging chamber (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging)  
5.2 Equilibrate sample at RT for 1 hour prior to light-sheet or confocal microscopy to minimize thermal drift during imaging.

**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The mouse stomach is a dense, lipid-rich soft organ (~20 mm scale) requiring strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—iDISCO+ excels in these aspects with established performance for T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM samples. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling relies on exogenous dyes (Alexa Fluor conjugates), which are fully compatible. PGP9.5 is a well-validated pan-neuronal marker for visualizing vagal and intrinsic nerve fibers throughout the gastric wall, while Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 robustly labels F-actin in smooth muscle layers (circular/longitudinal), providing essential structural reference for spatial mapping of neural projections relative to motility-related architecture.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP/tdTomato signals for long-range projection tracing across large, dense adult mouse brain tissue (~10 mm scale). Among compatible clearing methods, MACS is an aqueous-based protocol that robustly preserves fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and tdTomato), enables deep antibody penetration for structural labeling, and avoids organic solvents that quench or distort FP signals. To visualize local dendritic architecture in target regions (amygdala, PFC, thalamus, NAc), we supplement endogenous projection labeling with immunostaining against MAP2—a well-established dendritic marker—conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, which is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from EGFP/tdTomato. This combination allows simultaneous mapping of long-range axonal projections and local dendritic scaffolds without FP loss or significant tissue distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-MAP2)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-MAP2 primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal anti-MAP2, 1:500 dilution) in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) NGS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

3 Washing After Primary Antibody  
3.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 24 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining (Alexa Fluor 647)  
4.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300 dilution) in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) NGS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

5 Washing After Secondary Antibody  
5.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 24 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  

6 Tissue Optical Clearing (MACS)  
6.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 solution (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 solution (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 solution (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
7.1 Transfer cleared brain into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The mouse stomach is a dense, lipid-rich soft organ (~20 mm scale) requiring strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for this tissue tier, offering high clearing power, rapid processing, and excellent compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes—critical for dual-channel neural fiber labeling. Endogenous fluorescence is already absent (fixed tissue), so quenching is not a concern. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) and β-III Tubulin (a neuron-specific cytoskeletal marker) together provide complementary coverage of nerve trunks, branches, and fine terminals across all gastric wall layers. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are both highly compatible with iDISCO+, resistant to organic solvents, and enable low-background, high-signal dual-color imaging of the entire迷走神经 network.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for gastric tissue with hemoglobin/pigment)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (pre-blocking)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

5.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)

9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP/tdTomato signals and robust labeling of dendritic architecture across a large, lipid-rich adult mouse whole brain. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method that preserves fluorescent proteins without quenching, enables deep antibody penetration, and provides homogeneous refractive index (RI) matching with low background—addressing the prior SWITCH failure (which suffers from incomplete delipidation and poor FP retention under SDS-only conditions). MAP2 is a well-established pan-dendritic marker compatible with MACS and does not interfere with endogenous FP signals; conjugation to Alexa Fluor 647 ensures strong far-red signal retention in thick tissue. This combination supports high-resolution 3D imaging of long-range projections (via EGFP/tdTomato) and local dendritic morphology (via MAP2-AF647) within emotion-related circuits.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Labeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (e.g., chicken anti-MAP2, 1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 5 changes over 5 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-chicken IgY conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 5 changes over 5 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0: 20% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Incubation with final RI matching solution: MACS-R3 (50% vol/vol MXDA, 60% wt/vol sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.52) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer brain to fresh MACS-R3 in glass vial for long-term storage or immediate imaging (Temperature: 4 ℃ for storage; RT for imaging, protected from light)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP/tdTomato signals from genetically labeled projection neurons, which rules out solvent-based methods that quench fluorescent proteins (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). MACS is an aqueous, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically validated for whole adult mouse brains (~10 mm scale), preserves endogenous GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence with high fidelity, and enables deep penetration of immunolabeling reagents. To visualize local neuronal architecture (dendrites and neurites) in target regions like the thalamus or nucleus accumbens for spatial correlation with projection terminals, we add pan-neuronal structural labeling using anti-MAP2 (a dendritic marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647—a fluorophore compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from EGFP/tdTomato. This strategy fulfills both long-range axonal tracing (via endogenous signal) and local structural reference (via immunostaining) without FP quenching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for gentle rehydration after PFA fixation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with PBST containing 20% (vol/vol) DMSO and 0.3 M glycine for antigen retrieval and membrane permeabilization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling for Neuronal Structure  
2.1 Blocking with MACS blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or rabbit, 1:500 dilution) in MACS blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Washing with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100) to remove unbound primary antibody. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: anti-host IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300 dilution) in MACS blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Final washing with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100) to remove unbound secondary antibody. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  

3 Optical Clearing with MACS Reagents  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer cleared brain into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage and imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite; replace solution every 2 weeks if stored >1 month)  
4.2 Prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging, equilibrate sample in MACS-R2 at RT for at least 2 hours to minimize thermal drift and RI mismatch. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-c-Fos + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-NeuN + Alexa Fluor 568, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires mapping activity-dependent neuronal ensembles across the entire brain and preserving the spatial relationship between the tongue and brainstem nuclei involved in arousal-motor control. c-Fos is a well-established immediate early gene marker for recent neuronal activation, making it ideal for capturing anesthesia-awakening–induced activity. NeuN provides pan-neuronal context to distinguish activated neurons from non-neuronal cells. Given the large, dense, lipid-rich nature of intact mouse brain and tongue (T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM), a high-clearing-power solvent-based method is essential. iDISCO+ offers deep antibody penetration, strong delipidation, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes—critical since endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched during processing. TO-PRO-3 serves as a nuclear counterstain for anatomical registration without interfering with c-Fos/NeuN signals, and is compatible with iDISCO+ when used post-immunostaining. This combination enables robust 3D mapping of activated neural circuits with preserved morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing anti-c-Fos (1:500) and anti-NeuN (1:1000).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two additional times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle agitation)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two additional times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Nuclear Counterstaining  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 dilution from 1 mM stock).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

12 Re-dehydration  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

13 Refractive Index Matching  
13.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
13.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
13.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [C-FoS + Alexa Fluor 488, Npas4 (IEGs) + Alexa Fluor 568, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires simultaneous detection of two immediate early gene (IEG) products—C-Fos and Npas4—as functional markers of neuronal activation in deep brain nuclei (MTN, LC, PVT, NAcSh) across an intact mouse brain and tongue. iDISCO+ is selected because it provides strong delipidation and high clearing power for large, dense tissues like whole mouse brain (~1.5 cm) and tongue, enabling deep antibody penetration. It is established for tier T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM samples and compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 conjugates, which are robust under organic solvent processing. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in iDISCO+, so genetic reporters are avoided in favor of immunolabeling with validated anti–C-Fos and anti–Npas4 primary antibodies followed by Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondaries. TO-PRO-3 is included as a far-red nuclear counterstain compatible with iDISCO+ (unlike DAPI/Hoechst, which show signal loss or nonuniformity in solvent-based clearing) to aid whole-brain registration and cell density estimation without interfering with IEG channels.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented tongue tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti–C-Fos (e.g., Santa Cruz sc-52, 1:500) and anti–Npas4 (e.g., Synaptic Systems 229 003, 1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 three more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 three more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 in PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
9.2 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Repeat step 11.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, sealed.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

13 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Store samples immersed in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
13.2 Mount cleared brain and tongue in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires tracing two distinct somatosensory projection pathways across large, lipid-rich CNS tissues (3 cm spinal cord, thalamus, and cortical slabs). DiI and DiD are lipophilic carbocyanine dyes that stably incorporate into neuronal membranes and are ideal for long-range axonal tracing without requiring genetic manipulation or antibody penetration. uDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically validated for long-range neural projections in whole-mount mouse CNS (including spinal cord and brain), offering strong delipidation power, deep dye preservation, and compatibility with DiI/DiD fluorescence. It outperforms aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS) in clearing dense, myelinated tracts and enables whole-organ 3D imaging with minimal signal loss. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are not used per problem constraints, and DiI/DiD are explicitly permitted and optimal for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for spinal cord pigmentation)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for DiI/DiD pre-labeling stability; skip if dyes already applied in vivo)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Dye Application (if not pre-injected in vivo; otherwise skip to Step 5)  
4.1 Microinjection of DiI (2–5 mg/mL in ethanol) and DiD (2–5 mg/mL in ethanol) into distinct peripheral sensory ganglia or nerve endings under stereomicroscope, followed by incubation in 4% PFA at 4 ℃ for 7–14 days to allow anterograde transport.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7–14 days)  

5 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
5.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer cleared samples to glass vials filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite for imaging within 1 month)  
8.2 Mount samples in DBE-filled imaging chambers compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition of DiI (Ex/Em ~549/565 nm) and DiD (Ex/Em ~644/665 nm) signals.
