model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-c-Fos primary + Alexa Fluor 647 secondary, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, uniform labeling of functionally activated neurons across the entire mouse brain and tongue, with structural reference from tongue musculature. c-Fos is a canonical immediate early gene (IEG) marker for neuronal activation and is explicitly listed as a target-specific marker for “活化神经元.” Since iDISCO+ uses organic solvents that quench endogenous fluorescent proteins, we rely on immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated secondary antibodies, which are fully compatible with iDISCO+. Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 labels F-actin in tongue skeletal muscle fibers for anatomical reference and is compatible with iDISCO+ when applied post-clearing or during rehydration. TO-PRO-3 provides nuclear counterstain for gross anatomical registration without interfering with c-Fos signal (unlike DAPI/Hoechst, which are cautioned in solvent-based methods for IEG detection). iDISCO+ is established for large, dense tissues like whole mouse brain and tongue (T06 tier), offers strong delipidation for deep antibody penetration, and achieves high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented tissue; include for tongue if melanin present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.6 Incubation with 100% PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Permeabilization and Blocking  
5.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (wt/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Primary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with anti-c-Fos rabbit monoclonal antibody (e.g., Cell Signaling #2250) diluted 1:500 in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.2% heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

7 Washing  
7.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% heparin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Repeat 7.1 three more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

8 Secondary Antibody Staining  
8.1 Incubation with goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 diluted 1:500 in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.2% heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

9 Post-staining Washes  
9.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% heparin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Repeat 9.1 two more times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing for final RI matching)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Final Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching and Counterstaining  
12.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) DCM : dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
12.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE containing Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution) and TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 dilution).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
12.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

13 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with 100% (vol/vol) DBE, seal tightly.(Temperature: RT, protected from light, Time: until imaging)  
13.2 Equilibrate at RT for ≥1 hour before light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Justification:** The scientific goal requires dual detection of two immediate early genes (IEGs)—C-Fos and Npas4—to map activity-dependent neuronal ensembles across deep brain nuclei (MTN, LC, PVT, NAcSh) in intact mouse brain-tongue preparations. iDISCO+ is selected because it provides strong delipidation and high refractive index matching suitable for large, dense tissues like whole brain and tongue (T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM tier), enables deep antibody penetration via methanol-based dehydration and detergent-assisted permeabilization, and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 568 and Alexa Fluor 647—both robust synthetic fluorophores resistant to organic solvents used in iDISCO+. **Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD, NeuN (RBFOX3)+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity tracing of two distinct long-range somatosensory pathways through dense CNS tissue (spinal cord, thalamus, cortex) and precise 3D spatial comparison of their trajectories and terminal zones. DiI and DiD are lipophilic carbocyanine dyes ideal for anterograde/retrograde axonal tracing with minimal cross-talk (distinct emission spectra) and excellent compatibility with organic solvent–based clearing. uDISCO is selected because it provides strong delipidation and high refractive index matching for large, lipid-rich CNS samples (>15 mm), enabling deep imaging of long-range projections with minimal scattering. It preserves DiI/DiD fluorescence robustly and supports immunolabeling for nuclear markers like NeuN to delineate thalamic nuclei and cortical layers for anatomical registration—critical for determining convergence or segregation of pathways. Although uDISCO causes some tissue shrinkage, this is acceptable for relative spatial mapping when consistent across samples. Endogenous FPs are not used; thus, FP quenching by uDISCO is irrelevant.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Pre-Clearing Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual PFA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration for Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunolabeling (NeuN for nuclear reference)  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-NeuN (RBFOX3) diluted 1:500 in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Washing with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 diluted 1:500 in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.5 Washing with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

5 Dehydration Post-Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final RI matching and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires long-range tracing of somatosensory pathways using lipophilic carbocyanine dyes (DiI/DiD), which are highly compatible with organic solvent–based clearing methods. uDISCO is specifically established for large, dense CNS tissues (e.g., whole spinal cord and brain) and provides strong delipidation and high refractive index (RI) matching essential for deep imaging of 3 cm spinal cords and intact thalamocortical regions. Unlike aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS), uDISCO efficiently removes myelin lipids that impede transparency in white matter–rich tracts while preserving DiI/DiD fluorescence—both dyes are known to be stable in methanol and dichloromethane-based protocols. uDISCO also avoids the need for antibody labeling or Alexa Fluor incubation, aligning with the constraint to use only DiI/DiD as tracers. Its dehydration–delipidation–RI matching sequence ensures uniform clearing and low background, enabling reliable 3D reconstruction of overlapping/parallel sensory projections.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 ratio).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: overnight (12–16 hours))  

4 Post-Clearing Equilibration for Imaging  
4.1 Transfer tissue to fresh 100% (vol/vol) BABB in glass imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The target is sensory nerve fibers in lipid-rich mouse subcutaneous white adipose tissue (scWAT), requiring a clearing method with strong delipidation power and deep antibody penetration. uDISCO is established for high-lipid tissues (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier), provides excellent transparency and refractive index matching (>1.52), and supports robust immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor dyes. PGP9.5 is a validated pan-neuronal marker that reliably labels sensory nerve fibers in adipose tissue; co-staining with β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) enables discrimination of total neuronal architecture versus sensory-specific components. Both primary antibodies are compatible with organic solvent–based protocols when paired with Alexa Fluor 647/488, which are stable in uDISCO. Endogenous fluorescence is not relied upon, avoiding quenching issues.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if residual pigmentation observed)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunostaining)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) (1:500) in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing solution every 1–2 hours on day 1, then daily for 3 days total.  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.02% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times over 3 days (daily changes).  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 2:1 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in sealed amber glass vial until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (DyLight 594) for vasculature]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for lipid-rich tissues like scWAT, offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration essential for thick (1 cm³) samples. It effectively clears dense adipose tissue while preserving fine neural morphology. Since endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in organic solvents, we use immunolabeling: CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide) specifically labels peptidergic sensory nerve fibers, while PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) reveals the total innervation network. Alexa Fluor 647 and Alexa Fluor 488 are compatible with iDISCO+ and provide spectrally distinct, photostable signals for 3D quantification. Lectin conjugated to DyLight 594 (functionally equivalent to Alexa Fluor 594 in compatibility) is used as a vascular reference channel; though caution is noted for lectin in some contexts, its covalent labeling of endothelial glycocalyx survives iDISCO+ processing when applied pre-clearing. Nuclear dyes (DAPI/Hoechst) are avoided due to poor retention and incompatibility with quantitative neural morphometry in lipid-rich tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (reverse methanol series)  
1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody and Lectin Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:200), anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), and DyLight 594-conjugated Lectin (10 µg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

4 Washes Post Primary  
4.1 Incubation with wash buffer (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times, changing buffer every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

5 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (same as 3.1).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

6 Washes Post Secondary  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times, changing buffer every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Dehydration (methanol series)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Repeat step 7.5 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

9 Dichloromethane (DCM) Treatment  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, stored over molecular sieves).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Repeat step 9.1 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
10.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term storage <1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method with high delipidation power, ideal for lipid-rich tissues like scWAT (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier). It enables deep antibody and dye penetration into dense, thick samples (~1 cm³), which is essential for visualizing fine sensory nerve fibers throughout the entire fat depot. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy relies on exogenous immunostaining and lectin conjugates—compatible with iDISCO+. Alexa Fluor 568/647 are robust in organic solvents and provide strong signal for CGRP (sensory-specific) and PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal), while IB4-Lectin-Alexa Fluor 488 reliably labels vascular endothelial luminal surfaces without requiring transgenic reporters. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of CGRP⁺ fibers relative to pan-neuronal scaffolds and vasculature.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for lipid-rich tissue with residual heme)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (wt/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide (blocking buffer).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-CGRP (e.g., rabbit polyclonal, 1:200) + anti-PGP9.5 (e.g., mouse monoclonal, 1:500) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody + Lectin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) + goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in amber glass vial, sealed with Parafilm.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
12.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, avoiding air bubbles.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for lipid-rich tissues like scWAT, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging of dense adipose tissue. It enables excellent antibody penetration in thick samples and preserves Alexa Fluor 568/647 signals—both compatible with iDISCO+. CUBIC failed due to insufficient delipidation in high-lipid scWAT; switching to iDISCO+ addresses this by aggressive organic solvent-mediated lipid removal. CGRP is the canonical marker for peptidergic sensory nerve fibers in adipose tissue, while PGP9.5 (also known as UCHL1) is a pan-neuronal cytoplasmic marker that labels all neural processes, enabling dual visualization of sensory-specific vs. total innervation. Both require immunostaining (not endogenous FP), which aligns with iDISCO+’s requirement for dye/antibody labeling (as it quenches GFP/YFP). Nuclear counterstains are omitted per constraints and because they do not contribute to neural fiber quantification.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for scWAT to reduce autofluorescence)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-CGRP (e.g., rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (e.g., mouse monoclonal, 1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% donkey serum + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five more times (total 6 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 5% donkey serum + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage or immediate imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Mount tissue in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with DBE; seal to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for dense mineralized hard tissues like bone (T07 tier), enabling deep antibody and dye penetration into cranial and femoral bone, marrow cavities, and meninges. It effectively handles decalcified, lipid-rich, and pigmented samples while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes. PGP9.5 and β-III Tubulin are pan-neuronal/axonal markers essential for visualizing the full architecture of bone-innervating and meningeal nerves; Lectin labels vasculature to contextualize neurovascular relationships; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain without interfering with neural identity. Endogenous FPs are quenched by FDISCO, so all labeling must be via immunostaining or compatible synthetic dyes—this strategy satisfies that constraint while ensuring specific, high-contrast 3D mapping of neural pathways through bone microenvironments.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days for skull; 10 days for femur)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Permeabilization and Blocking  
5.1 Incubation with PBST containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Primary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:200), anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500), and biotinylated Lectin (1:200) in PBST with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 2% (vol/vol) normal goat serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

7 Washing  
7.1 Wash with PBST containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 12 hours over 3 days)  

8 Secondary Antibody and Nuclear Counterstain  
8.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated streptavidin (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), in PBST with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 2% (vol/vol) normal goat serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

9 Post-staining Washes  
9.1 Wash with PBST containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 12 hours over 3 days, protected from light)  

10 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

11 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer samples to glass vials filled with fresh ECi and store at RT in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
12.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for dense mineralized tissues like bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), enabling deep antibody penetration into cranial and femoral bone while preserving fine neural morphology with minimal distortion relative to other solvent methods. It efficiently clears both cortical bone and marrow-containing cavities, critical for visualizing intraosseous nerve networks. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched, so all labeling must be dye- or antibody-based—this aligns with the requirement to definitively identify CGRP⁺ sensory fibers (via anti-CGRP) and pan-neuronal architecture (via anti-PGP9.5). IB4-Lectin (conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488) labels non-peptidergic sensory nerve terminals and vascular endothelium in bone, providing complementary structural context without substituting for CGRP identity. DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain for marrow and meningeal cellularity. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568/647, DAPI) are compatible with FDISCO per domain records.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:200), anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times with fresh wash buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500), donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), plus IB4-Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (10 µg/mL), in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times with fresh wash buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for dense hard tissues like bone and compatible with thick composite samples (cranial bone, femur, meninges, marrow). It enables deep antibody/dye penetration while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes (Alexa Fluor series) and lectins—critical for labeling CGRP⁺ sensory fibers (target-specific), pan-neuronal PGP9.5, and vascular lumen via IB4/Lectin. Endogenous FPs are quenched, but this is irrelevant as labeling relies on immunostaining and exogenous dyes. FDISCO’s rapid clearing kinetics and high refractive index matching suit 3D mapping of fine neural-vascular interfaces in mineralized tissue. Mild decalcification precedes clearing to preserve morphology without destroying epitopes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
0 Pre-Clearing Decalcification (for fixed bone-containing samples)  
0.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days; change solution every 2 days)  

1 Immunolabeling (post-decalcification, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500) + anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  
1.4 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes, 4-hour intervals)  
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-mouse (1:500), plus Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4 (10 µg/mL), all in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
1.6 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

3 Delipidation & Bleaching (optional if pigmentation present)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

4 Rehydration (for RI matching transition)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with FDISCO-RI matching solution: 62.5% (wt/vol) iodixanol (OptiPrep) + 12.5% (wt/vol) urea + 25% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, adjusted to RI ≈ 1.46.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with final FDISCO mounting medium: 88% (wt/vol) iodixanol + 12% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water (RI ≈ 1.52).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

6 Storage & Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with final FDISCO mounting medium.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ in dark for up to 2 weeks)

我在进行小鼠颅骨透明化实验时遇到问题：按照标准 BoneClear protocol 操作，固定后进行甲醇梯度脱水和 bleaching，然后进行远红荧光二抗孵育和 RI matching。结果骨组织仍然不透明，无法观察骨内结构，且远红信号很弱。该流程可能缺少充分脱钙、骨基质软化、深层透化和长时间抗体渗透，也可能因 bleaching 或脱水步骤过强导致抗原和荧光信号受损。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合矿化骨组织脱钙、骨髓和脑膜结构保留、神经纤维双信号检测、低背景、深层抗体渗透和三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for mineralized hard tissues (e.g., bone) and provides deep antibody penetration while preserving far-red fluorescence—addressing the weak signal and poor transparency observed with BoneClear. Unlike aqueous methods, FDISCO efficiently removes lipids and residual pigments without requiring harsh bleaching that damages antigens. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 568/647 conjugates, enabling robust dual-channel detection of CGRP⁺ sensory fibers (target-specific) and pan-neuronal PGP9.5⁺ networks. The protocol includes controlled decalcification and extended permeabilization to enhance antibody access to dense bone matrices, while avoiding nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) that are cautioned against for PGP9.5/CGRP targets per domain guidance.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Rehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  
1.3 Gradual rehydration: sequential incubation in 50%, 30%, 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:200) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:400) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 14 days with gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours × 3 changes, 8 hours per change)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  
4.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours × 3 changes, 8 hours per change)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Sequential dehydration in 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
5.2 Final dehydration in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

6 Delipidation and Bleaching (Optional, if residual pigment present)  
6.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours in dark)  
6.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  
7.3 Incubation with FDISCO mounting solution (100% ethyl cinnamate, ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes until tissue becomes transparent)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store samples in ECi at RT in sealed glass vials protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)  
8.2 Mount in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.56).

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized hard tissues like mouse femur, tibia, and skull, enabling efficient decalcification-coupled clearing while preserving bone marrow cavity architecture. It provides strong delipidation and high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.52), essential for deep imaging in dense bone. Unlike SWITCH—which fails to clear mineralized bone adequately—BoneClear integrates EDTA-based decalcification with organic solvent-based clearing, ensuring antibody penetration into the marrow niche. Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 are compatible with BoneClear’s solvent protocol and offer bright, photostable signals for TH (catecholaminergic) and NPY (peptidergic) sympathetic nerve fibers without cross-reactivity or quenching. This strategy avoids reliance on endogenous fluorescence (quenched in solvent methods) and focuses on robust immunolabeling of target-specific markers required for spatial mapping in the hematopoietic microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4, in PBS) containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation and solution change every 2 days)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated twice)  

3 Immunolabeling (performed after dehydration to enhance antibody penetration)

6.1 Incubation with BoneClear mounting medium (benzyl benzoate : diphenyl ether = 5:3 vol/vol, RI ≈ 1.52).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)

7.1 Transfer samples to glass-bottom imaging chambers filled with fresh BoneClear mounting medium.(Temperature: RT, storage in dark until imaging)  
7.2 Seal chamber edges with nail polish to prevent evaporation and solvent leakage prior to light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like mouse long bones and skull, enabling deep antibody penetration into enclosed bone marrow cavities. It effectively removes lipids and decalcifies mildly during processing, critical for accessing marrow-resident structures. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling relies on robust immunostaining with Alexa Fluor dyes—compatible with FDISCO—and includes DAPI for nuclear reference. TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is the gold-standard marker for catecholaminergic sympathetic fibers, while NPY (neuropeptide Y) labels peptidergic sympathetic terminals; dual labeling allows direct comparison of their spatial distributions. CD31 delineates bone marrow vasculature for distance analysis relative to neural elements. FDISCO’s rapid clearing kinetics (days vs. weeks) and compatibility with these fluorophores make it optimal for quantitative 3D mapping in hard tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 vol 30% H₂O₂ + 5 vol MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-TH (1:200), anti-NPY (1:200), and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit (1:400), Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-guinea pig (1:400), and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat (1:400), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin (from Lycopersicon esculentum) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for mineralized hard tissues like mouse bone (femur, tibia, skull), enabling deep antibody and dye penetration into dense bone marrow cavities. It preserves synthetic fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) and lectin conjugates while efficiently removing lipids and matching refractive index for high-resolution 3D imaging. The chosen labeling strategy directly targets the scientific goals: TH and NPY immunostaining identifies catecholaminergic and peptidergic sympathetic nerve fibers, respectively, while tomato lectin (Lycopersicon esculentum) robustly labels vascular endothelial luminal surfaces in bone marrow without requiring transgenic reporters. All fluorophores are compatible with FDISCO as per domain knowledge.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-NPY (1:200) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and anti-guinea pig IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400), plus Lycopersicon esculentum Lectin–Alexa Fluor 647 (10 µg/mL), all diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, with 4 buffer changes)

9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D mapping of neural fibers (including fine axons and bundles) in relation to tumor epithelium within a dense, heterogeneous pancreatic tumor (~12 mm). iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM samples, offering strong delipidation power for deep antibody penetration into fibrotic and lipid-rich tumor stroma, rapid clearing kinetics, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched by iDISCO+, so we use immunolabeling: PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal cytoplasmic marker highly specific for peripheral nerves in PNI contexts) paired with Alexa Fluor 647 for robust far-red signal retention; Pan-Cytokeratin labels epithelial tumor cells to delineate tumor boundaries and assess spatial relationships with nerves. Both antibodies are validated in iDISCO+ protocols and avoid nuclear counterstains that lack target specificity per problem constraints.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (PBST + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:200) and anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin + 3% (vol/vol) donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (same as 5.1).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 568, CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, specific labeling of both pan-neuronal (PGP9.5) and sympathetic-specific (TH) fibers within a dense, fixed pancreatic tumor (~12 mm scale), alongside a tumor epithelial boundary marker (CK19). iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM samples, offering strong delipidation and high clearing power essential for dense fibrotic tumor tissue, while enabling deep antibody penetration. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 488/568/647-conjugated antibodies—ideal for multiplexed immunolabeling of PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal), TH (sympathetic identity), and CK19 (tumor ductal epithelium for spatial reference). This combination allows precise 3D mapping of sympathetic vs. total nerve distribution relative to tumor architecture.

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense tissues like brain tumors, enabling deep penetration of antibodies and dyes while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor conjugates. It is established for whole mouse brain blocks (5–12 mm) and compatible with both Lectin (for intravascular perfusion labeling of functional vasculature) and anti-CD31 immunostaining (for structural endothelial network). Lectin injected pre-fixation labels only perfused vessels, directly reporting functional perfusion; CD31 reveals total vascular endothelium. FDISCO preserves Alexa Fluor 488/647 signals robustly and achieves rapid, high-clarity clearing suitable for light-sheet imaging of vascular architecture and perfusion overlap.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Pre-labeling (performed prior to fixation, but included for completeness)  
1.1 Intracardiac perfusion with 100 µg/mL Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)  
1.2 Immediate post-perfusion fixation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

2 Post-fixation Stabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunostaining for CD31  
4.1 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with rat anti-CD31 primary antibody (1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
4.4 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.5 Wash with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Transfer to fresh 100% ECi for storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store sample immersed in ECi in glass vials protected from light at RT.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (灌注血管腔面标记) + CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647 (血管内皮结构)]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method established for dense, lipid-rich adult mouse brain tissue (5–12 mm scale), offering strong delipidation and deep dye penetration while preserving exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes and lectin conjugates. It is compatible with both Lectin (for labeling perfused vascular lumens via intracardiac perfusion prior to fixation) and anti-CD31 immunostaining (to visualize total endothelial architecture). This dual-labeling strategy enables discrimination between functional (perfused) and structural (total) vasculature—critical for assessing vascular normalization (e.g., restored perfusion, reduced blind ends). FDISCO minimizes fluorescence quenching compared to iDISCO+, supports long-term sample stability in DBE, and achieves high transparency in days, suitable for light-sheet imaging of whole tumor blocks.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D mapping of neural fibers (PGP9.5, a pan-neuronal marker) and tumor epithelial structures (Pan-Cytokeratin, a robust epithelial/carcinoma marker) in a dense, fixed mouse pancreatic tumor (~12 mm scale). iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM samples, offering strong delipidation power for deep antibody penetration, rapid clearing kinetics, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses exogenous Alexa Fluor–conjugated antibodies, which are fully compatible. DAPI is included cautiously as a nuclear counterstain to aid spatial registration, with limited but acceptable signal retention in iDISCO+. This combination enables precise quantification of nerve–tumor spatial relationships across tumor core, invasive front, and residual normal tissue.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 568, Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep antibody penetration into dense, lipid-rich pancreatic tumor tissue (~12 mm scale) with strong delipidation and background reduction to visualize faint neural signals and define tumor boundaries for PNI analysis. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based method for this tissue tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), offering high clearing power, effective decoloration (via H₂O₂/methanol), and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Endogenous fluorescence is quenched in iDISCO+, so all targets must be labeled via immunostaining—PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker) and TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, sympathetic-specific) provide the required dual neural labeling, while Pan-Cytokeratin robustly marks epithelial tumor cells to delineate tumor borders and enable PNI assessment. Alexa Fluor 488/568/647 are all compatible with iDISCO+ and allow multichannel 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Decoloration / Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (or species-matched blocking serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), anti-TH (1:500), anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:300) in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample contains endogenous tdTomato/RFP signal in breast cancer cells, which must be preserved; thus, an aqueous, fluorescence-preserving clearing method is essential. MACS is established for whole mouse brain (5–12 mm scale), provides strong clearing power for dense tissue, maintains endogenous FP signal (including tdTomato), enables deep antibody penetration, and causes minimal morphological distortion—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of invasion patterns. Pan-Cytokeratin is a pan-epithelial marker that specifically labels carcinoma cells of epithelial origin (e.g., breast cancer), allowing unambiguous distinction of true metastatic foci from autofluorescence or non-specific signals. Alexa Fluor 647 is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from tdTomato, enabling dual-channel validation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (prior to clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., clone AE1/AE3) diluted 1:200 in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:300 in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in MACS-R2 at RT for at least 2 hours to ensure optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato/RFP fluorescence from breast cancer cells while enabling specific immunolabeling of epithelial identity via an epithelial marker. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method established for adult mouse brain tissue (5–12 mm scale), fully compatible with endogenous red fluorescent proteins (tdTomato/RFP) and Alexa Fluor dyes, and supports deep antibody penetration without quenching or requiring hazardous solvents. Among epithelial markers, Pan-Cytokeratin is a canonical pan-epithelial cytokeratin marker that robustly identifies carcinoma cells of epithelial origin, fulfilling the requirement to validate tumor cell identity beyond fluorescence alone. Alexa Fluor 647 is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from tdTomato, enabling dual-channel 3D imaging of tumor location (tdTomato) and epithelial phenotype (Pan-Cytokeratin).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., clone AE1/AE3 or equivalent) diluted 1:200 in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:300 in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in water, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle agitation)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite, protected from light)  
3.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in MACS-R2 at RT for at least 2 hours to ensure optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato/RFP signal and specific immunolabeling of epithelial-derived metastatic cells using Pan-Cytokeratin. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method established for whole mouse brain (5–12 mm scale), preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins including tdTomato/RFP, enables deep antibody penetration, and minimizes tissue distortion—addressing the user’s prior issues of structural damage and weak reference signals. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., uDISCO, iDISCO+), MACS avoids FP quenching and excessive shrinkage. Pan-Cytokeratin is a validated target-specific marker for epithelial cancer cell identification in brain metastasis contexts and is compatible with Alexa Fluor 568, which is stable in MACS and spectrally distinct from tdTomato for dual-channel validation of tumor identity and boundary delineation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (mouse monoclonal, e.g., clone AE1/AE3), diluted 1:200 in antibody dilution buffer (2% NDS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 12 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568, diluted 1:300 in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 12 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue to fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in MACS-R2 for at least 6 hours to ensure optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
