**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato/RFP (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato/RFP signal from metastatic breast cancer cells in intact mouse brain (~12 mm scale), which rules out solvent-based methods that quench fluorescent proteins (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). MACS is an aqueous, high-refractive-index clearing method established for whole adult mouse brains, compatible with endogenous RFP/tdTomato, and supports deep penetration of antibodies and lectins. Pan-Cytokeratin (a pan-epithelial marker) validates the epithelial identity of tdTomato+ metastatic cells, while IB4 lectin labels vasculature to assess perivascular invasion patterns. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for brain parenchymal architecture without interfering with RFP or antibody signals. MACS offers excellent structural preservation, minimal tissue distortion, and compatibility with multi-channel fluorescence imaging (light-sheet/confocal).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling and Nuclear Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody and lectin cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:300) + Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated IB4 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (10 μg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue into fresh MACS-R2 in a glass imaging chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
3.2 Seal chamber to prevent evaporation; store at 4 ℃ if imaging delayed beyond 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires simultaneous visualization of functional perfused vasculature (via intravascular lectin labeling) and total endothelial structure (via CD31 immunostaining) in dense, fixed glioma tissue. iDISCO+ provides strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging in lipid-rich brain tumors, with excellent compatibility for Alexa Fluor 488/647 dyes. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous FPs, our labeling relies on exogenous, covalently bound fluorescent conjugates that are stable under organic solvent processing. Lectin injected pre-fixation labels only perfused vessels, while anti-CD31 reveals the full endothelial network—enabling quantitative comparison of perfusion status vs. structural integrity. iDISCO+’s established efficacy for whole mouse brain blocks (5–12 mm) ensures uniform clearing without the incomplete dehydration and skipped steps that compromised the prior FDISCO attempt.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for glioma autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody staining)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (wt/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-CD31)  
5.1 Incubation with anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (wt/vol) NGS + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat or anti-hamster IgG (matching host of CD31 antibody), diluted 1:500 in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (wt/vol) NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Post-staining Dehydration  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-TH + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for mineralized hard tissues like mouse femur (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody penetration after decalcification and delipidation, preserves fine neural morphology with minimal distortion relative to other solvent methods, and is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and DAPI. Since endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in solvent clearing, primary antibodies against CGRP (sensory neuron marker) and TH (sympathetic neuron marker) conjugated to photostable Alexa Fluor dyes provide specific, high-contrast labeling essential for distinguishing sensory vs. sympathetic innervation patterns in the complex bone microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA disodium salt in PBS, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Permeabilization  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Repeat wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Immunolabeling  
4.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 minutes each at RT.  
4.2 Blocking: incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
4.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-CGRP (1:500) and anti-TH (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  
4.4 Wash: 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes over 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per change)  
4.5 Secondary antibody incubation: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)  
4.6 Wash: 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes over 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per change)  
4.7 Nuclear counterstain: incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.8 Final wash: PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Re-dehydration for Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Optical Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.5 Incubation with fresh 100% ECi. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi for long-term storage at RT in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
7.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. Ensure no air bubbles. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like bone (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration while preserving fine neural morphology with minimal autofluorescence. It efficiently clears intact mouse femurs (~15 mm) within days and is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes. CGRP is the canonical marker for peptidergic nociceptive sensory fibers in bone pain models; PGP9.5 (UCHL1) serves as a pan-neuronal marker to delineate the entire intraosseous nerve network. IB4 (isolectin B4) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 labels vasculature and non-peptidergic sensory endings, providing spatial reference for perivascular innervation without interfering with CGRP/PGP9.5 signals. Endogenous fluorescence is not relied upon (FDISCO quenches FPs), so all labeling uses robust, photostable Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies or directly labeled lectins, ensuring high signal-to-noise in 3D imaging of bone microenvironments.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation and solution change every 48 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:500) and mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  
2.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, with buffer changes every 8 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), plus Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated IB4 (10 μg/mL), all in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light)  
2.5 Washing with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, protected from light)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
4.2 Washing with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Final Clearing and Storage  
6.1 Incubation with fresh 100% ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
6.2 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi for long-term storage and light-sheet/confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample is a small (5 mm-scale) fixed mouse embryonic trunk at E9.5–E10.5 with endogenous tdTomato fluorescence driven by Wnt1-Cre, which must be preserved. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves red fluorescent proteins like tdTomato while enabling deep antibody penetration—critical for detecting nuclear Sox10 in migrating neural crest cells. Among FP-compatible aqueous methods (MACS, CUBIC, ScaleS, Ce3D), MACS offers faster clearing kinetics for small whole samples and superior morphological preservation compared to CUBIC (which can cause swelling) or ScaleS (slower). Sox10 immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 647 provides high-contrast, far-red labeling compatible with tdTomato and minimizes spectral crosstalk during multichannel imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Staining (performed before clearing to ensure nuclear epitope accessibility)  
1.1 Rehydration: Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubation with PBST + 10% normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.5% DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation with anti-Sox10 (e.g., R&D Systems AF2864 or equivalent, 1:200 dilution) in PBST + 5% NDS + 0.5% DMSO. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Washing: Incubation with PBST (3 changes, 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.5 Secondary antibody incubation: Incubation with donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400 dilution) in PBST + 5% NDS + 0.5% DMSO, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Post-staining wash: Incubation with PBST (4 changes, 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage and imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite; store protected from light)  
3.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in MACS-R2 at RT for 1 hour to minimize thermal drift during light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-TH + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (TRITC-conjugated) or IB4 (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated)]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like intact mouse long bones (T07_HARD_TISSUE tier). It enables deep penetration of antibodies and lectins into bone cortex and marrow while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes (Alexa Fluor series) and lectin conjugates. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched, but this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on immunostaining and exogenous dyes. FDISCO achieves rapid, high-RI matching suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging of 15 mm-long femurs. The chosen markers directly address the scientific goals: CGRP for nociceptive sensory fibers, TH for sympathetic fibers, PGP9.5 as a pan-neuronal marker to map total innervation, and Lectin/IB4 to label vascular endothelial luminal surfaces without requiring CD31 immunostaining (which may suffer from poor bone penetration). All fluorophores are compatible with FDISCO per domain records.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-CGRP (1:200), anti-TH (1:200), anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  
1.4 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, gentle shaking)  
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-mouse, Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-chicken (all 1:500) + TRITC-Lectin (10 µg/mL) or Alexa Fluor 647-IB4 (5 µg/mL) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  
1.6 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, protected from light)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Dehydration (repeat after rehydration if counterstain applied)  
5.1 Repeat steps 2.1–2.5  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Sigma-Aldrich, 112372-100G) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to fresh ECi in glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage, protected from light)  
7.2 Mount in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.558)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample is a small (5 mm) fixed mouse embryonic trunk at E9.5–E10.5, requiring preservation of endogenous tdTomato fluorescence from Wnt1-Cre;tdTomato lineage tracing and deep immunolabeling for the nuclear transcription factor Sox10 to identify undifferentiated neural crest/glial progenitors. Ce3D is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method established for small whole embryonic tissues (T03 tier), fully compatible with tdTomato and Alexa Fluor dyes, supports excellent antibody penetration into dense embryonic mesenchyme, and minimizes morphological distortion—critical for spatial mapping of migrating neural crest cells in structures like DRGs and sympathetic chains. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), Ce3D does not quench fluorescent proteins, and unlike SeeDB2 or ClearT2, it enables robust deep-tissue immunostaining for nuclear targets like Sox10.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (prior to clearing)  
1.1 Rehydrate fixed embryo trunks in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Permeabilize with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Block in blocking buffer (PBS + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-Sox10 (e.g., R&D Systems MAB2864 or equivalent), diluted 1:200 in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash thoroughly with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.6 Incubate with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse or anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:500 in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.7 Wash thoroughly with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 7.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 7.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C solution (75% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 7.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer samples to Ce3D-RI matching solution (88% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Store and image in Ce3D-RI matching solution at 4 ℃ in the dark until light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for dense, mineralized hard tissues like mouse long bones (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It provides strong delipidation and high refractive index matching, enabling deep antibody penetration into bone marrow cavities and periosteal/endosteal niches—critical for visualizing sparse intraosseous nerve fibers. Unlike aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, Ce3D), FDISCO achieves faster and more complete clearing of calcified bone without requiring prolonged incubation. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on exogenous primary antibodies conjugated to compatible Alexa Fluor dyes (488/568/647), all confirmed compatible with FDISCO. Crucially, FDISCO preserves fine neural morphology and allows simultaneous multiplexed detection of CGRP⁺ (sensory), TH⁺ (sympathetic), and PGP9.5⁺ (pan-neuronal) fibers—fulfilling the scientific goal of comparing neuroplasticity across bone compartments in a bone cancer pain model. EDTA decalcification is included upfront to enable antibody access without compromising epitope integrity when performed under controlled conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

5 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500), anti-TH (1:500), anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) in blocking solution, with gentle rotation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Wash with PBST containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 24 hours, change buffer daily)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500), donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Wash with PBST containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 24 hours, change buffer daily)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The sample is a small (≤5 mm) fixed mouse embryonic trunk at E9.5–E10.5 expressing tdTomato under Wnt1-Cre, requiring preservation of endogenous red fluorescence while enabling deep immunolabeling for Sox10 to resolve neural crest migration and differentiation states. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that preserves tdTomato signal integrity, supports robust antibody penetration in dense embryonic tissue, and is established for small whole-mount samples of this size class. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for tissue registration and cell density reference without interfering with tdTomato or Alexa Fluor 488 channels. Alexa Fluor 488 is compatible with MACS and offers high signal-to-noise for Sox10 detection.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (performed prior to clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against Sox10 (e.g., rabbit anti-Sox10, 1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 changes every 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (e.g., donkey anti-rabbit IgG, 1:400 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 changes every 2 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate light-sheet or confocal imaging (RI ≈ 1.51)  
3.2 For short-term storage (<1 week), keep sample immersed in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark  
3.3 For long-term storage (>1 week), replace MACS-R2 weekly to prevent crystallization or microbial growth

**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method specifically validated for small whole embryonic tissues (1–5 mm) that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins like tdTomato without quenching, enables deep antibody penetration for nuclear transcription factors such as Sox10, and minimizes tissue distortion—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of delicate neural crest migration paths. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), Ce3D avoids methanol dehydration and harsh delipidation that degrade FP signal and disrupt embryonic morphology. The use of Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-Sox10 ensures bright, photostable labeling compatible with Ce3D’s refractive index matching and co-imaging with tdTomato.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (perform before clearing to ensure antibody penetration)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 10% normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rabbit anti-Sox10 (1:200 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, with 4 buffer changes)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-A solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-B solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Matching Solution (80% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with Ce3D-Matching Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (store at 4 ℃ if imaging delayed beyond 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated), IB4 (Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated), DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically optimized for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like placenta, offering strong delipidation and hemoglobin removal while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes. It enables deep penetration into dense vascular networks and achieves whole-organ transparency in days. Lectin and IB4 (both isolectin B4) bind specifically to endothelial glycocalyx of perfused vasculature, labeling functional lumenal surfaces of maternal-fetal exchange vessels without requiring genetic reporters or lengthy immunostaining. Co-labeling with DAPI provides nuclear context for tissue architecture. FDISCO is compatible with all selected fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 568/647 and DAPI), unlike iDISCO+ which risks quenching or poor DAPI retention. This combination ensures high-fidelity 3D reconstruction of the entire villous tree, including terminal capillaries and perfusion status.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (Hemoglobin Removal)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 part 30% H₂O₂ + 5 parts methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for Lectin/IB4 Staining)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Vascular Lumen Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with staining solution containing 10 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin) and 10 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated IB4 (*Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) in PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (wt/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
4.2 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
4.3 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Dehydration (Post-Staining)  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation & Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, stored over molecular sieves).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (from *Lycopersicon esculentum*) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 for functional perfused vasculature; anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody for endothelial structural morphology]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like placenta (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier), offering strong delipidation, deep dye/antibody penetration, and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores including Alexa Fluor dyes and lectin conjugates. It maintains high signal-to-noise for both vascular lumen labeling (via intravascular lectin perfusion) and immunostained endothelial markers. Lectin-AF647 binds specifically to glycocalyx on luminal surfaces of perfused vessels, directly reporting functional perfusion status, while CD31 immunostaining reveals all endothelial-lined vascular structures regardless of perfusion—enabling precise spatial comparison in labyrinth, maternal-fetal interface, and marginal zones. FDISCO is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 and preserves lectin binding integrity, unlike some harsher solvent methods.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Based Functional Vessel Labeling (Perform prior to fixation if possible; if post-fixation, use passive incubation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50 µg/mL *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in PBS containing 1 mM CaCl₂ and 1 mM MnCl₂ (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours with gentle agitation)  

2 Post-Fixation (if not already fixed)  
2.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Repeat wash twice (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

4 Immunostaining for CD31  
4.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
4.4 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Repeat wash three times (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
4.6 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 diluted 1:500 in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  
4.7 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.8 Repeat wash three times (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation and Bleaching  
6.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours in the dark)  

7 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
7.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Sigma-Aldrich, 112302) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.5 Incubation with fresh 100% ECi (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Store sample in 100% ECi at RT in the dark until imaging (stable for weeks)  
9.2 Mount in glass-bottom dish filled with ECi for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.558)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (functional perfused lumen), IB4 (functional perfused lumen), CD31/PECAM1 + Alexa Fluor 647 (structural endothelium)]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method optimized for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like placenta (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier). It preserves exogenous fluorophores including Alexa Fluor dyes and is compatible with lectin/IB4 labeling, enabling dual assessment of functional perfusion (via intravascular lectin/IB4 binding to glycocalyx of patent vessels) and structural endothelial architecture (via anti-CD31). Its rapid clearing kinetics suit 10–12 mm whole placental samples, and it achieves high refractive index matching (~1.56) ideal for light-sheet imaging of deep vascular networks in the labyrinth and villous tree.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Based Vascular Lumen Labeling (if not pre-perfused)  
1.1 Retrograde perfusion via maternal uterine artery or fetal umbilical artery with ice-cold PBS containing 50 µg/mL DyLight 649-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin and 50 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4 in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.2 Post-perfusion fixation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Post-fixation Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Immunostaining for Structural Endothelium  
3.1 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rat anti-mouse CD31/PECAM1 (1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Washing with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.5 Final wash with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Rehydration (for optional nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
6.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh batch).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.5 Final incubation with fresh 100% ECi for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

8 Storage and Imaging  
8.1 Store sample immersed in ECi at RT in sealed glass vial protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
8.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) with 638 nm laser excitation for Alexa Fluor 647/Lectin/IB4 signals; collect z-stacks through entire placental thickness (3–4 mm).

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PSD95 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-resolution synaptic imaging in thick brain tissue (1–2 mm), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration while preserving fine dendritic and spine morphology with minimal distortion. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes (including AF488 and AF647) and effectively clears dense hippocampal tissue. PSD95 is a canonical excitatory postsynaptic density scaffold protein that specifically labels functional excitatory synapses; MAP2 robustly labels dendritic shafts of CA1 pyramidal neurons, enabling precise spatial mapping of synaptic puncta along dendritic compartments. This combination fulfills the requirement for target-specific labeling of both excitatory postsynaptic structures and dendritic architecture without relying on endogenous fluorescent proteins (which FDISCO preserves but are not specified in the sample).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: rabbit anti-PSD95 (1:200) and chicken anti-MAP2 (1:500) diluted in PBST + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Repeat step 3.1 three more times, total of 4 washes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

4 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) and donkey anti-chicken IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) in PBST + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

5 Post-labeling Washes  
5.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Repeat step 5.1 three more times, total of 4 washes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Repeat step 6.4 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Bleaching  
7.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

8 Equilibration in Dichloromethane (DCM)  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
9.2 Transfer sample to fresh ECi for long-term storage or immediate imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PSD95 + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Homer1 + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D visualization of two excitatory postsynaptic scaffold proteins (PSD95 and Homer1) alongside dendritic architecture in thick (1–2 mm) fixed mouse hippocampal CA1 tissue. Ce3D is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method established for thick brain slices (0.5–3 mm), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal distortion—critical for spatial analysis of puncta distribution across CA1 strata. It supports deep penetration of antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor dyes (488/568/647), which are fully compatible per the knowledge base. MAP2 is selected as a dendritic marker to delineate pyramidal cell layers, radiatum, and distal dendritic zones, enabling precise layer-specific correlation of synaptic protein signals. Nuclear dyes (e.g., DAPI) are omitted as they do not substitute for structural synaptic or dendritic labeling per problem constraints.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) containing 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for washing fixed tissue blocks (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with Ce3D-P1 solution (25% (wt/vol) N-methyldiethanolamine, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) for permeabilization and initial clearing (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (Ce3D-P1 supplemented with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-PSD95 (1:200), mouse anti-Homer1 (1:200), chicken anti-MAP2 (1:500) diluted in Ce3D-P1 + 2% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
2.3 Washing with Ce3D-P1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: goat anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400), goat anti-mouse IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400), goat anti-chicken IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) in Ce3D-P1 + 2% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
2.5 Washing with Ce3D-P1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Final Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-R1 solution (40% (wt/vol) N-methyldiethanolamine, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with Ce3D-R2 solution (50% (wt/vol) N-methyldiethanolamine, 40% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer cleared tissue blocks into glass vials filled with Ce3D-R2 for long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
4.2 Mount samples in Ce3D-R2 within imaging chambers compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin or *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 568 secondary antibody]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-lipid, pigment-rich tissues like placenta, offering strong delipidation and hemoglobin removal while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes and lectin conjugates. It effectively reduces blood-derived background and enables deep penetration of antibodies and lectins into dense vascular networks. Lectin perfusion labels functional, perfused vascular lumens in vivo, while anti-CD31 immunostaining reveals total endothelial morphology—including non-perfused or collapsed vessels—enabling comprehensive 3D reconstruction of the villous tree vasculature. FDISCO is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 568 and 647, and supports lectin labeling without quenching, unlike iDISCO+. The combination provides dual-channel discrimination of structural endothelium (CD31) and functional perfusion status (lectin), critical for analyzing maternal-fetal interface hemodynamics.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Based Lectin Labeling (Perform prior to fixation if possible; if post-fixation only, skip to step 2 and rely on passive diffusion)  
1.1 If live perfusion feasible: Transcardially perfuse pregnant dam at E18.5 with 10 mL PBS followed by 10 mL of 50 µg/mL *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin–Alexa Fluor 647 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min perfusion)  
1.2 Immediately dissect placenta and fix in 4% PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

2 Post-Fixation Tissue Preparation (If no perfusion performed, begin here with fixed placenta)  
2.1 Wash placenta in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  

3 Immunolabeling for CD31  
3.1 Permeabilize in PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Block in PBS + 5% normal goat serum + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.3 Incubate with rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody (1:200 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.4 Wash in PBS + 0.2% Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  
3.5 Incubate with goat anti-rat IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 secondary antibody (1:500 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.6 Wash thoroughly in PBS + 0.2% Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 2 changes)  

6 Rehydration (for optional nuclear counterstain; omit if background is concern)  
6.1 Optional: Rehydrate through descending methanol series (80%, 60%, 40%, 20% in PBS, 30 min each) then incubate with TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 in PBS) if nuclear context needed.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Re-dehydrate through ascending methanol series back to 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per step)  

7 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min × 2 changes)  
7.3 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma 112392) for final RI matching.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount cleared placenta in ECi in glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary tube, avoiding bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for ≤1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PSD95 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-Homer1 + Alexa Fluor 568, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-resolution synaptic imaging in thick brain tissue (1–2 mm), offering strong delipidation power for dense regions like CA1 while preserving fine structures such as dendritic spines and synaptic puncta with minimal distortion. It maintains compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes (488/568/647), which are ideal for multiplexed labeling of excitatory postsynaptic scaffolds. PSD95 and Homer1 are canonical, functionally distinct markers of excitatory postsynaptic densities—PSD95 enriched in mature synapses, Homer1 in metabotropic glutamate receptor-associated complexes—fulfilling the requirement to distinguish functional subtypes. MAP2 provides robust dendritic arbor labeling without nuclear or non-specific background. FDISCO avoids endogenous FP quenching issues by relying on antibody-conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes, ensures deep penetration into 1–2 mm blocks, and achieves RI matching (~1.52) compatible with high-NA oil or silicone objectives for confocal/light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB) containing 2% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-PSD95 (1:200), anti-Homer1 (1:200), anti-MAP2 (1:500) in PBST (0.1 M PB, 0.5% Triton X-100, 10% normal goat serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with PBST (0.1 M PB, 0.5% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times with solution change every 2 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse (1:500), Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500), Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-chicken (1:500) in PBST with 10% normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

5 Post-labeling Wash  
5.1 Incubation with PBST (0.1 M PB, 0.5% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)  

7 Delipidation and Bleaching  
7.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours in dark)  

8 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing validation; skip if proceeding directly to clearing)  
*(Skipped per FDISCO protocol—proceed directly to dichloromethane)*  

9 Organic Solvent Transition  
9.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) mixture of 100% methanol and dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, repeated twice)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Imaging Mounting  
11.1 Transfer tissue into fresh ECi in glass-bottom imaging chamber and seal for immediate light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PSD95 + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Homer1 + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D mapping of excitatory postsynaptic puncta (PSD95 and Homer1) along CA1 pyramidal neuron dendrites. MAP2 is a well-established dendritic marker that robustly labels the somatodendritic compartment without labeling axons, enabling precise spatial registration of synaptic puncta relative to dendritic shafts and spines. iDISCO+ was selected because it provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration in dense 1–2 mm brain blocks, is established for this tissue tier (T02_THICK_SLICE_0P5_3MM), and preserves Alexa Fluor dyes (488/568/647) with high compatibility. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling relies entirely on immunostaining with compatible synthetic fluorophores, avoiding this limitation. The method achieves rapid clearing with minimal residual background, critical for distinguishing true synaptic puncta from noise in dendritic regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if autofluorescence is high)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine, 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum in PBS): anti-PSD95 (1:200), anti-Homer1 (1:200), anti-MAP2 (1:500) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  

5 Washing  
5.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Repeat step 5.1 five more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

6 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in antibody dilution buffer: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (1:400), Alexa Fluor 568 anti-rabbit (1:400), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-chicken (1:400) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

7 Post-Secondary Washing  
7.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Repeat step 7.1 five more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

8 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Delipidation  
9.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until clear)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Mount cleared tissue in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with DBE, sealed to prevent evaporation (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark for ≤1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-HCN4 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 568, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense, lipid-rich mouse organs like the heart (T05 tier), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for visualizing the sparse cardiac conduction system. It effectively reduces myocardial autofluorescence through methanol dehydration and H₂O₂ bleaching, directly addressing the high background issue. Although it quenches endogenous FPs, our labeling uses exogenous Alexa Fluor dyes, which are fully compatible with iDISCO+. HCN4 specifically labels sinoatrial/atrioventricular nodal pacemaker cells, while Cntn2 robustly marks Purkinje fibers; both are validated target-specific markers for the conduction system. Phalloidin-AF488 labels F-actin in cardiomyocytes to preserve fiber orientation without interfering with conduction-specific signals. This combination enables simultaneous 3D mapping of conduction pathways and myocardial architecture with minimal distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) in PBT + 5% donkey serum + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)

8.2 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-HCN4 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 568, Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method with high delipidation power and excellent penetration for dense tissues like the intact mouse heart (~15–20 mm), enabling deep immunolabeling of internal conduction structures (SA node, AV node, His-Purkinje system). It is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes (488, 568, 647), which are photostable and ideal for multi-channel 3D imaging. HCN4 specifically labels pacemaker cells in the SA/AV nodes, Cntn2 robustly marks Purkinje fibers, and Phalloidin–AF488 provides high-resolution F-actin contrast to delineate myocardial fiber orientation in atria, ventricles, and septum—critical for spatial correlation analysis. Endogenous fluorescence is not required; all signals derive from antibody/dye labeling, which aligns with iDISCO+’s quenching profile.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-HCN4 (1:200) and anti-Cntn2 (1:200) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat 6.1 five more times (total 6 washes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Hu C/D + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The intact mouse colon (6–8 cm) is a large, dense, lipid-rich tubular organ requiring a high-clearing-power method with deep antibody penetration and minimal structural collapse to preserve layered architecture and distinguish myenteric (Auerbach’s) from submucosal (Meissner’s) plexuses. uDISCO is established for T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM samples, offering rapid, strong delipidation and high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging of whole organs. It preserves Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 signals robustly. Hu C/D labels neuronal nuclei specifically in the ENS, while PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) highlights the full axonal network; together they enable quantification of ganglion density, size, and fiber connectivity across proximal-distal regions. **Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HuC/D + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for long tubular organs (T06 tier) with high lipid content like the colon, offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. It effectively clears 6–8 cm samples while preserving gross morphology sufficient to distinguish myenteric (Auerbach’s) and submucosal (Meissner’s) plexuses. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched, so target-specific immunolabeling is required. HuC/D and PGP9.5 are well-validated pan-neuronal markers for ENS neuron somata and fibers; dual labeling ensures robust identification of ganglia (HuC/D+) and their interconnecting fiber tracts (PGP9.5+). Phalloidin labels F-actin in smooth muscle layers, providing structural context to delineate muscularis externa (circular/longitudinal layers) and submucosa, enabling precise layer assignment of neural elements. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568/647) are compatible with iDISCO+ per method-fluorophore guidelines.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution: anti-HuC/D (1:500), anti-PGP9.5 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody + Phalloidin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies and Phalloidin in blocking solution: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated Phalloidin (1:200).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation

10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
