**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for thin tissue slices ≤500 μm, offering rapid and high-efficiency clearing with excellent compatibility for Alexa Fluor dyes and deep antibody penetration—critical for visualizing dense renal cortical structures like the glomerular filtration barrier. It preserves fluorescence of exogenous dyes while quenching endogenous FPs, making it ideal for immunolabeling-based strategies. Nephrin and Podocin are target-specific structural markers of the slit diaphragm and podocyte foot processes, respectively; labeling them with spectrally distinct, FDISCO-compatible Alexa Fluor conjugates ensures high signal-to-noise ratio and precise 3D reconstruction of the filtration barrier.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation in blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) rabbit polyclonal antibody (1:200) and anti-Podocin (NPHS2) goat polyclonal antibody (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  

3 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol), protected from light.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

6 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; omitted here per marker cautions)  
*(Skipped to avoid DAPI/Hoechst due to incompatibility with Nephrin/Podocin labeling context)*  

7 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer tissue to a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh ECi for immediate light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD19+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method compatible with small intact lymphoid organs (~3 mm), preserving endogenous fluorescence and enabling deep antibody penetration without significant tissue distortion—critical for maintaining lymph node architecture. It supports both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 conjugates, which are highly compatible and photostable. B220 (PTPRC) is a pan-B cell marker that robustly labels follicles, while CD19 provides complementary B-cell specificity and enhances delineation of germinal centers when co-stained. This dual-marker strategy ensures precise visualization of B-cell zones and germinal center organization in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with anti-B220 (PTPRC) primary antibody (1:200 in blocking solution) and anti-CD19 primary antibody (1:200 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
2.2 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 4 changes)  

3 Secondary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (for B220) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (for CD19), each at 1:300 in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
3.2 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 4 changes)  

4 Optical Clearing with MACS  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
5.2 Store at 4 ℃ in MACS-R2 if not imaged immediately (stable for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based high-refractive-index clearing method established for thick (0.5–3 mm) dense tissues like mouse cardiac apex, offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 568 and 647, enabling robust dual-channel labeling. α-SMA is a well-validated marker for activated myofibroblasts in cardiac fibrosis, and CD31 specifically labels endothelial cells of the coronary vasculature, allowing precise 3D reconstruction of vascular trees and their spatial relationship to fibrotic regions. FDISCO avoids quenching of these synthetic fluorophores and provides rapid clearing suitable for small tissue blocks.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with anti-α-SMA (1:200) and anti-CD31 (PECAM1) (1:100) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

3 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  

6 Rehydration (for FDISCO-compatible RI matching)  
6.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with FDISCO-RI matching solution (FDISCO-Mount: ethyl cinnamate / DBE mixture, RI ≈ 1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Transfer to fresh FDISCO-Mount for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store sample immersed in FDISCO-Mount in glass-bottom imaging chamber sealed with vacuum grease.(Temperature: RT, protected from light)  
8.2 Proceed to light-sheet or confocal microscopy within 7 days for optimal signal integrity.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato fluorescence for retrograde tracing of long-range projections, which rules out solvent-based clearing methods that quench fluorescent proteins (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). Among FP-compatible aqueous methods established for adult mouse whole brain (T04 tier), MACS offers strong clearing power, deep antibody penetration, minimal distortion, and compatibility with both tdTomato and Alexa Fluor 647. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a pan-neuronal axonal marker ideal for visualizing axon scaffold structure alongside tdTomato-labeled projection neurons. MACS supports efficient immunolabeling in thick tissue without requiring hydrogel embedding or harsh solvents, aligning with the need for speed and simplicity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash fixed brain 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 5% normal donkey serum (NDS), 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted 1:500 in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 12 hours in PBST (0.2% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:300 in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 days with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 12 hours in PBST (0.2% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer cleared brain into fresh MACS-R2 for final equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Mount sample in glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for light-sheet microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for thick tissue slices (0.5–3 mm), offering excellent preservation of lung alveolar architecture with minimal distortion—critical for visualizing delicate air sacs. It supports deep penetration of both lectin and anti-CD31 antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor dyes, enabling dual visualization of functional perfused vasculature (via intravascular lectin labeling) and endothelial cell boundaries (via CD31 immunostaining). DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cellular context without compromising structural integrity. Ce3D preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor 488/647 and DAPI, aligns with low-toxicity handling, and is compatible with light-sheet or confocal imaging after RI matching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Perfusion Labeling  
1.1 Transcardial perfusion of live mouse with ice-cold PBS followed by 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.2 Immediately post-perfusion, inject 50 µg/mL Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in PBS into the right ventricle to label perfused vascular lumens.(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes circulation, then fix in situ for additional 1 hour)  
1.3 Dissect lung and cut into 1.5 mm thick blocks using a vibratome or scalpel in cold PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: immediate processing)  

2 Post-fixation and Washing  
2.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS for post-fixation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

3 Immunostaining for CD31  
3.1 Block in blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubate with primary antibody: rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1) at 1:200 dilution in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
3.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubate with secondary antibody: goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 at 1:400 dilution in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
3.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  

4 Nuclear Counterstaining  
4.1 Incubate with DAPI at 1 µg/mL in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

5 Ce3D Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
6.1 Transfer tissue to Ce3D-Matching Solution (88% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.47).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Store and image in Ce3D-Matching Solution at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 week)

It effectively clears dense embryonic tissue and supports deep antibody penetration. The dual-target labeling strategy uses β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), a pan-neuronal marker labeling early axons and mature neurites, and Sox10, a transcription factor marking neural crest-derived lineages including peripheral glia and developing cranial/spinal ganglia—both critical for visualizing the full spectrum of embryonic nervous system development. **Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Stabilin-2 + Alexa Fluor 488, Lyve-1 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method established for dense, lipid-rich whole mouse organs like the liver (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM tier). It preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes and supports deep antibody penetration—critical for labeling the intricate, low-expression liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) network. Stabilin-2 and Lyve-1 are two well-validated, LSEC-specific markers that together comprehensively label the hepatic sinusoidal vasculature without relying on pan-endothelial markers like CD31, which may underrepresent LSECs. Both primary antibodies can be reliably detected with Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, which are fully compatible with FDISCO per method–fluorophore compatibility data. FDISCO also achieves high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet microscopy while minimizing signal quenching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Perfuse adult mouse transcardially with ice-cold PBS followed by 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: perfusion until liver appears pale and firm)  
1.2 Dissect whole liver and post-fix in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Block in blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: rat anti-Stabilin-2 (1:200) and goat anti-Lyve-1 (1:200) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
2.3 Wash thoroughly in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
2.5 Wash thoroughly in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 12 hours)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 2 hours)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Rehydration (for optional intermediate check; skip if proceeding directly to clearing)  
5.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Refractive Index Matching (FDISCO Clearing)  
6.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 2 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer cleared liver to fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi in glass imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD45+Alexa Fluor 488, CD11b+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for hard tissues like bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), offering strong delipidation and decalcification-compatible processing that enables deep antibody penetration into mineralized bone marrow. It preserves synthetic fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor dyes) while quenching endogenous fluorescent proteins—thus requiring exogenous labeling, which aligns with the need for specific immune cell markers. CD45 is a pan-leukocyte marker ideal for labeling all bone marrow immune cells, while CD11b (Itgam) specifically labels myeloid-lineage cells (monocytes, macrophages, neutrophils, dendritic cells). Both are well-established in murine bone marrow immunophenotyping and compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent environment when conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488/647, which are explicitly listed as FDISCO-compatible.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CD45 (rat anti-mouse, 1:200) and anti-CD11b (rat anti-mouse, 1:200) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Secondary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (repeat twice). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

5 Delipidation and Decalcification Support  
5.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osteocalcin + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin/IB4 pre-labeled vasculature]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for hard tissues like bone, offering excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent signals (including pre-labeled Lectin/IB4), minimal tissue distortion, and deep antibody penetration—critical for visualizing the dense trabecular architecture and marrow vasculature. It avoids harsh organic solvents that could strip or quench lectin-based vascular labeling. Osteocalcin is a specific late-stage osteoblast marker that labels both osteoblasts and their secreted matrix, while CD31 robustly labels endothelial cells of bone vasculature. Using Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 ensures compatibility with Ce3D’s fluorescence-preserving chemistry and enables spectral separation from pre-existing IB4/Lectin signal (typically conjugated to green/red fluorophores). This combination allows simultaneous 3D mapping of bone matrix, vasculature, and osteolineage cells without over-decalcification or structural collapse.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to ensure complete fixation if not already fully fixed. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

2 Permeabilization and Decalcification (Mild)  
2.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4), supplemented with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation; change solution every 48 hours)  

3 Blocking and Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with wash buffer: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total, with 6 buffer changes at 4-hour intervals)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) and donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300), diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light, with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total, with 6 buffer changes)  

7 Clearing with Ce3D Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 0.3% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with Ce3D-M (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 35% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, RI ≈ 1.48) until sample becomes transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample into fresh Ce3D-M in a glass-bottom imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ for up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for dense hard tissues like adult mouse molars (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), enabling deep antibody and dye penetration while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes (Alexa Fluor series) and lectins. It efficiently clears mineralized dental tissue without requiring decalcification. PGP9.5 is a pan-neuronal marker robustly expressed in dental pulp nerves; TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) specifically labels sympathetic fibers. IB4 (isolectin B4 from Griffonia simplicifolia) binds to endothelial glycans and reliably labels murine microvasculature in pulp tissue. All three primary labels are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent environment and do not rely on endogenous fluorescent proteins (which FDISCO quenches). This triple-labeling strategy fulfills the requirement to distinguish general vs. sympathetic innervation and visualize vascular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody mix: anti-PGP9.5 (1:200), anti-TH (1:200), and biotinylated IB4 (10 µg/mL), all diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing buffer each time.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Streptavidin Conjugate Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody mix: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400), donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400), and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), all diluted in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing buffer each time.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ≈ 1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
